a13_0080733.text: Okay. Stand by and I'll get it out.

a13_0080733.speaker: Brand
a13_0080733.text: Okay. On checklist G/8-2 under step 5, there's a statement, 'disable all jets on two adjacent quads,' and that's what we were referring to when we called up saying 'disable quads A and B.' So that's all fine; however, going down now to step 7 where it says 'enable all jets,' we hoped that you didn't think we meant leave A and B disabled there. In that case, it's as written. All jets should be enabled. Over.

a13_0080733.speaker: Swigert
a13_0080733.text: Okay. Our checklist has 'all jets' scratched out, and it says 'enable couples on all axes.' So what we'll do is - we'll re-establish this thing and come down to that step 7, and we'll enable all jets. That means enable quads A and B. Is that right?

a13_0080733.speaker: Brand
a13_0080733.text: That's affirm. You'll have A, B, C, and D enabled for step 7.

a13_0080733.speaker: Swigert
a13_0080733.text: Okay, real fine. I'll start on it now.

a13_0080733.speaker: Brand
a13_0080733.text: Okay. Understand you're going to re-establish it. [Long pause.]

a13_0080733.speaker: Haise
a13_0080733.text: And Vance, on that picture, I was all set to shoot it just a little before you called, and the Earth hasn't showed up in the window yet. I don't know if we got too far off the bellyband or what.

a13_0080733.speaker: Brand
a13_0080733.text: Roger. On the photo, you'll probably have to re-establish the attitude for PTC and then whenever it comes into the window again, why we'll just be standing by for the photo. [Pause.]

a13_0081949.speaker: Brand
a13_0081949.text: Roger, You're coming in a little weak. Have a recommended roll rate for this PTC, if you could copy.

a13_0081949.speaker: Brand
a13_0081949.text: Okay. Recommend that you put in R1 the following: 03750, and that should give you exactly a rate of 0.3 degrees per second. Over.

a13_0081949.speaker: Swigert
a13_0081949.text: Okay, 03750. Is plus or minus our choice? [Pause.]

a13_0081949.speaker: Brand
a13_0081949.text: Roger. The same direction you rolled last time, which I believe is plus.

a13_0082506.speaker: Swigert
a13_0082506.text: Hey, Vance, would you monitor our rates and kind of give us an idea of when you think they're stable enough to start PTC.

a13_0082506.speaker: Brand
a13_0082506.text: Rog, Jack. We'll take a look and let you know as soon as they look stable enough.

a13_0082506.speaker: Swigert
a13_0082506.text: Okay. I've got quads A and B disabled here.

a13_0082506.speaker: Swigert
a13_0082506.text: Have they come up with an idea of how much fuel I used on the docking and also the P23 session at 5 hours or 6 hours. [Pause.]

a13_0082506.speaker: Brand
a13_0082506.text: I think we can give you something. Stand by a minute.

a13_0082506.speaker: Brand
a13_0082506.text: Okay. It's looking good so far as RCS consumables are concerned, Jack. You're standing about 20 pounds above the curve right now. Looking at the TD&E, you expended 65 pounds or - Stand by - 55 pounds, correction on that.

a13_0082506.speaker: Brand
a13_0082506.text: And 14 pounds on P23s. You used a little more out of quad A than out of the others.

a13_0082506.speaker: Swigert
a13_0082506.text: Hey, could you say again the TD&E fuel? We've got a different - we all heard different things.

a13_0082506.speaker: Brand
a13_0082506.text: I said 65 and then corrected that to 55 pounds.

a13_0083136.speaker: Brand
a13_0083136.text: Okay, Jim. Your rates look good. It's okay to start the roll again, if you'd like.

a13_0090247.speaker: Haise
a13_0090247.text: Okay. Stand by for a mark on another picture.

a13_0092458.speaker: Swigert
a13_0092458.text: Okay, Vance, and I guess I'll try to be slower on that Verb 37.

a13_0092458.speaker: Brand
a13_0092458.text: Yes. Actually slower or faster, either one, I guess. Well, yeah, slower. It's a very unusual thing to have that happen.

a13_0092458.speaker: Haise
a13_0092458.text: Okay. And, Houston, stand by for a mark on another picture.

a13_0092458.speaker: Swigert
a13_0092458.text: Okay, Vance; we've completed that procedure, and let me know if everything was okay. [Pause.]

a13_0092458.speaker: Brand
a13_0092458.text: Okay, thank you. We'll let you know if anything isn't okay. I'm sure it's good now. [Pause.]

a13_0092458.speaker: Haise
a13_0092458.text: Tell G&C and Guido thanks a lot for keeping good track of me, there.

a13_0092458.speaker: Brand
a13_0092458.text: Rog. They're right on the ball. [Long pause.]

a13_0092458.speaker: Brand
a13_0092458.text: And, 13, Houston. If you would like, we can let you know about every 2 minutes before the Earth should be coming into your window. We think we've got it pegged down pretty well now, and you won't have to look for it so much. Do you want that?

a13_0092458.speaker: Haise
a13_0092458.text: Yeah. That would be fine, Vance.

a13_0092458.speaker: Brand
a13_0092458.text: And, 13, Houston. Guido says the bits are reset - rather, are set.

a13_0094558.speaker: Brand
a13_0094558.text: It's time for Fred to start looking for the Earth, should be coming by in about a couple of minutes.

a13_0094558.speaker: Lovell
a13_0094558.text: Okay. He's got his head out there right now.

a13_0094558.speaker: Haise
a13_0094558.text: Yeah. You've got that pretty well pegged, man. There it be.

a13_0094558.speaker: Haise
a13_0094558.text: Yeah. I guess so. In a minute, you're going to hear my kitchen timer ding, and that also says the Earth is there.

a13_0094558.speaker: Haise
a13_0094558.text: Okay. Stand by, Vance, for our countdown. [Pause.]

a13_0094558.speaker: Brand
a13_0094558.text: Rog. We're enjoying Fred's music there. [Pause.]

a13_0094558.speaker: Haise
a13_0094558.text: Yeah, I kind of like it too, Vance. [Pause.]

a13_0094558.speaker: Brand
a13_0094558.text: Yeah, we - we didn't hear much of it, though.

a13_0100338.speaker: Swigert
a13_0100338.text: Okay, Vance, we did another EMS null bias test and the - it went from 100.0 to 101.8 in 100 seconds.

a13_0100609.speaker: Brand
a13_0100609.text: Jack, like to verify, was that 100 to 100.8 or 101.8?

a13_0100609.speaker: Brand
a13_0100609.text: The Earth's coming up in the window again in 1 to 2 minutes.

a13_0100609.speaker: Swigert
a13_0100609.text: He's got it. You're right again. [Long pause.]

a13_0100609.speaker: Swigert
a13_0100609.text: Okay, stand by for a mark here.

a13_0100609.speaker: Brand
a13_0100609.text: Apollo 13, Houston. We have a CSM state vector to send you. Request P00 and Accept at your convenience. [Long pause.]

a13_0100609.speaker: Swigert
a13_0100609.text: Okay, Vance. There's P00 and Accept.

a13_0102931.speaker: Haise
a13_0102931.text: Looks like picture-taking time again. [Long pause.]

a13_0102931.speaker: Brand
a13_0102931.text: Okay, Earth should be coming into view.

a13_0102931.speaker: Brand
a13_0102931.text: Earth starting to look pretty small now?

a13_0102931.speaker: Swigert
a13_0102931.text: Well, looking at here, Vance, it's hard to be convinced it's even the Earth. All we see is water and clouds. [Pause.]

a13_0102931.speaker: Brand
a13_0102931.text: Well, I guess that's what we want. We want pictures of weather, right, clouds.

a13_0102931.speaker: Swigert
a13_0102931.text: Yeah, about half of it's covered with clouds.

a13_0103729.speaker: Swigert
a13_0103729.text: Okay, Vance. Are you copying the torqueing angles of the P52 option 3? [Long pause.]

a13_0103729.speaker: Brand
a13_0103729.text: That's affirm - that's affirm, but stand by.

a13_0103729.speaker: Brand
a13_0103729.text: Okay. We've got 'em. Go ahead and torque 'em, Jack.

a13_0103729.speaker: Swigert
a13_0103729.text: Okay. That was stars 20 and 27 and star-angle difference is five balls, and the time at torquing would be 10 hours, 40 minutes, 15 seconds.

a13_0103729.speaker: Brand
a13_0103729.text: 1 hour [means 10 hours], 40 minutes and 15 seconds; 20 and 27 stars; and five balls. Roger.

a13_0105133.speaker: Brand
a13_0105133.text: Time to look out your window for us again.

a13_0105908.speaker: Brand
a13_0105908.text: Jim, we're coming up on a handover between sites. You might lose comm momentarily.

a13_0105908.speaker: Lovell
a13_0105908.text: Okay. Understand handover, we might lose the comm.

a13_0111352.speaker: MCC
a13_0111352.text: Apollo 13, Houston.

a13_0111352.speaker: Swigert
a13_0111352.text: Go ahead.

a13_0111352.speaker: MCC
a13_0111352.text: You should have the Earth coming into view here shortly.

a13_0111352.speaker: Swigert
a13_0111352.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a13_0111352.speaker: Haise
a13_0111352.text: We got a new CapCom now. [Long pause.]

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: No, I changed my voice. [Long pause.]

a13_0111352.speaker: Haise
a13_0111352.text: Mark.

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Roger. Copy.

a13_0111352.speaker: Lovell
a13_0111352.text: That was negative, Houston. Say again.

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: We got your mark, Jim.

a13_0111352.speaker: Lovell
a13_0111352.text: Okay.

a13_0111352.speaker: Haise
a13_0111352.text: Hey, you still there, Vance?

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Rog. Go ahead.

a13_0111352.speaker: Haise
a13_0111352.text: I guess the world really does turn. I can see some of my landmasses now. It must be Australia down near the bottom and I guess we haven't really figured out what's over the - to the left. It must be some part of Asia. China, probably.

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Hey, maybe the fact that you verified that the Earth really turns, we can call this Haise's Theory, huh? [Pause.]

a13_0111352.speaker: Haise
a13_0111352.text: Very good, Vance. Very good.

a13_0111352.speaker: Lovell
a13_0111352.text: It's looking good for you, Vance.

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: No, seriously. Very interesting, we can see on the map now that you're between Guam and Hawaii and a little bit north, and you're almost out 60,000 miles [110,000 km].

a13_0111352.speaker: Swigert
a13_0111352.text: Yeah. I just did a P21 and we had 55,900 [103,500 km]. [Pause.]

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Okay. That's pretty good.

a13_0111352.speaker: Swigert
a13_0111352.text: I'll let you look at it again here. [Pause.]

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Incidentally, we're looking at a replay of your TD&E stuff here and the TV looks pretty good. First chance some of us had had to see it. [Long pause.]

a13_0111352.speaker: Swigert
a13_0111352.text: Okay, Vance. In R1, there's our altitude in tens of miles, 55,290 [102,400 km]. [Pause.]

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Okay.

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Apollo 13, Houston.

a13_0111352.speaker: Lovell
a13_0111352.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Okay. Looking at our computations back here, we show you about 55,450 [nautical miles, 102,690 km] and going out rapidly now.

a13_0111352.speaker: Lovell
a13_0111352.text: Well, HAL might be a little bit off.

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Okay.

a13_0111352.speaker: Swigert
a13_0111352.text: We have a sign underneath our LEB DSKY that 'my name is HAL.'

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: I can't imagine how that got there. [Pause.] Just remember, you have to be nice to HAL.

a13_0111352.speaker: Swigert
a13_0111352.text: We will. [Pause.]

a13_0111352.speaker: Swigert
a13_0111352.text: I think this PTC's going to work out good. I been watching it here for the last hour here.

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Good. It's looking good here. [Pause.]

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Good Lord!

a13_0111352.speaker: Lovell
a13_0111352.text: Houston, 13.

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: 13, Houston. You're very weak. Please repeat.

a13_0111352.speaker: Lovell
a13_0111352.text: Vance, to our calculations, we have taken about 10 Earth window photography pictures. I see nothing coming up here except to close the waste stowage vent here in a little while. I was thinking about getting squared away to bed down for the evening pretty soon. [Pause.]

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Okay. That sounds good, Jim. FAO here would like to request just one more picture before you bed down, if you don't mind.

a13_0111352.speaker: Lovell
a13_0111352.text: Okay. We'll come through with one more picture.

a13_0111352.speaker: Brand
a13_0111352.text: Okay.

a13_0113033.speaker: Brand
a13_0113033.text: A couple of items, Jim. The first is, the time for closing the waste stowage vent is 12:24. If you turn in before that time, why it's okay as far as we're concerned down here to close it before that time, just before you go to bed. The second point, we have some results on the P23s, and, if Jack's interested, we could give him the corrected altitudes we're getting, and so forth.

a13_0113033.speaker: Brand
a13_0113033.text: Okay. This is preliminary results, but it will give you some indication. Corrected altitude is turning out to be 17 plus or minus 4 kilometers, and the fact that it's plus or minus 4 kilometers indicates that you're being very consistent in judging the altitude. The effective altitude is turning out to be 10 plus or minus 12 kilometers. Comments are that, as I said before, you're being consistent on the horizon selection. The substellar point error is averaging 15 arc-minutes and if you could hold the rates to a minimum, you might shoot for 5 arc-minutes. That's the only comment there. Over.

a13_0113033.speaker: Swigert
a13_0113033.text: Okay. We'll try doing it better next time.

a13_0113530.speaker: Brand
a13_0113530.text: Okay, Jack, this is the last time for the Earth coming into view in about 1 to 2 minutes.

a13_0113530.speaker: Swigert
a13_0113530.text: Okay. I got my photographer looking out there.

a13_0113530.speaker: Brand
a13_0113530.text: 13, Houston. I just corrected. Actually, the Earth will come into view more times. It's just that we're [garbled] to the photography. Over.

a13_0113530.speaker: Brand
a13_0113530.text: Roger. We copy, and could you give us the frame number on that last picture, please?

a13_0113530.speaker: Haise
a13_0113530.text: Okay. We've been writing them all down, Vance, as we went, but that one turned out to be 29.

a13_0113530.speaker: Haise
a13_0113530.text: Okay, Jack says I can't read the counter very well. It should be 28 based on our start frame.

a13_0113530.speaker: Brand
a13_0113530.text: 13, Houston. Understand, though, the number showing that you read on the camera was 28. Is that affirm?

a13_0113530.speaker: Haise
a13_0113530.text: Yes. The readability of that thing is like, you know, half a frame one way or the other; so, 28, I think, is a good number.

a13_0114157.speaker: Haise
a13_0114157.text: I'll have to not wear it out before Jack gets there.

a13_0114157.speaker: Brand
a13_0114157.text: Sounds like that music's a pretty nice thing to have on a long voyage.

a13_0115928.speaker: Brand
a13_0115928.text: Fred, did you get any Master Alarms up there about 5 or 10 minutes ago? Folks thought they saw some here and they were curious about it.

a13_0115928.speaker: Haise
a13_0115928.text: Ah, yeah. We got another O 2 Flow High on - I guess it was about 5 minutes ago.

a13_0115928.speaker: Swigert
a13_0115928.text: I think, Vance, what - what the people down there might have been seeing is our testing.

a13_0115928.speaker: Brand
a13_0115928.text: Rog. Testing the Caution and Warning? [Pause.]

a13_0115928.speaker: Swigert
a13_0115928.text: Yeah. We were rigging a little siren device over the Master Alarm, and we were running a test on it.

a13_0115928.speaker: Brand
a13_0115928.text: Okay. Good enough. And anytime you're ready to copy, I've got a PAD, P37 block data.

a13_0120815.speaker: Lovell
a13_0120815.text: We're starting our presleep checklist and no medication.

a13_0120815.speaker: Brand
a13_0120815.text: Okay. The Doc says very good. [Long pause.]

a13_0120815.speaker: Lovell
a13_0120815.text: And, Houston, is there any onboard readouts that you don't have from us. [Pause.]

a13_0120815.speaker: Brand
a13_0120815.text: Stand by 1. We need the LM/CM Delta-P for one thing, and I'll check back in a minute with the others.

a13_0120815.speaker: Lovell
a13_0120815.text: Okay. And we still have the vent valve open. We'll close it one of the last things and I'm looking at LM/CM Delta-P right now and I see 0.5 in psi indicated.

a13_0120815.speaker: Brand
a13_0120815.text: Only other readouts we need are those on page 3-13 of the Flight Plan. Bat C, Pyro Bat A, Pyro Bat B, RCS A, B, C, and D readings, and DC Indicator select Main A or B.

a13_0120815.speaker: Haise
a13_0120815.text: And, Vance, we're still charging Bat B. Did you want to dispense with that in a few minutes? [Pause.]

a13_0120815.speaker: Swigert
a13_0120815.text: Okay, Vance, I've got your readouts on page 3-13 of the Flight Plan.

a13_0120815.speaker: Swigert
a13_0120815.text: Okay, Bat C is 37, Pyro Bat A is 37, Pyro Bat B is 37; RCS A, 94 percent; B, 95 percent; C, 93 percent; D, 96 percent. [Pause.]

a13_0120815.speaker: Brand
a13_0120815.text: Okay. In answer to the battery-charging question, I calculate it should be fully charged at 12:35. Play that one, though, the same as the waste vent. If you want to do it earlier because you're turning in, why that's fine with us.

a13_0120815.speaker: Haise
a13_0120815.text: Okay, we'll continue on with a few other things we got to get done, and just before turning in, we'll check with you, and you can remind us then.

a13_0121717.speaker: Swigert
a13_0121717.text: Houston, Apollo 13. Give me a call when you're ready for E-memory dump.

a13_0121717.speaker: Brand
a13_0121717.text: This is Houston, 13. You were weak. Please repeat.

a13_0121717.speaker: Swigert
a13_0121717.text: Okay, Vance, give me a call when you're ready for our E-memory dump. [Long pause.]

a13_0121717.speaker: Brand
a13_0121717.text: Okay, 13. We're not quite ready yet. We'll give you a call when we're ready.

a13_0121717.speaker: Swigert
a13_0121717.text: Okay, Vance. I understand you're ready.

a13_0121717.speaker: Brand
a13_0121717.text: Negative, GUIDO isn't quite ready yet.

a13_0121717.speaker: Swigert
a13_0121717.text: Okay. I thought I heard you call us.

a13_0121717.speaker: Brand
a13_0121717.text: But we're ready now, Jack, so GUIDO says he's ready to take it.

a13_0123433.speaker: Lovell
a13_0123433.text: Okay, Vance. Requesting clearance now to turn the vent valve back to Close again, and also the battery charge, Off.

a13_0123433.speaker: Brand
a13_0123433.text: Roger. That's fine with us, Jim. Proceed.

a13_0124105.speaker: Brand
a13_0124105.text: We think the spacecraft's looking in good shape. Nobody has any comment down here before you hit the hay.

a13_0124105.speaker: Swigert
a13_0124105.text: Okay. How do they think we stand on the way of consumables so far? [Pause.]

a13_0124105.speaker: Brand
a13_0124105.text: You're looking in good shape in all respects - consumables-wise.

a13_0124737.speaker: Brand
a13_0124737.text: Just the last comment, Jack. Would you clear Hal, please, so he doesn't burn his lights out there tonight?

a13_0124737.speaker: Swigert
a13_0124737.text: No, I - I was just - Yeah, I will do this for you.

a13_0124737.speaker: Brand
a13_0124737.text: And we'll see you in the morning, huh?

a13_0124737.speaker: Swigert
a13_0124737.text: Okay. It'll be just a minute or two yet. We have to finish up a couple more chores.

a13_0124737.speaker: Haise
a13_0124737.text: What do you mean? It is morning.

a13_0124737.speaker: Brand
a13_0124737.text: It's been a long day, huh?

a13_0231114ag.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231114ag.text: Good morning, 13. This is Houston. How are you?

a13_0231114ag.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231114ag.text: Read you loud and clear. We had a fairly good night's sleep.

a13_0231114ag.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231114ag.text: Okay. Real fine. At your leisure, you can give us radiation reports, I guess. And, we're getting a consumables update together for you, and a few other little details whenever you're ready to talk. About the only major thing on the spacecraft is that it's been getting farther away.

a13_0231114ag.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231114ag.text: Okay. Well, that's to be expected, I guess.

a13_0231538.speaker: Haise
a13_0231538.text: And we're starting to charge battery A, Houston.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Rog on battery A, Fred. EECOM says battery B looks real good.

a13_0231538.speaker: Haise
a13_0231538.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Houston, 13.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Go ahead.

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Okay. For information, Fred was on comm last night; and he was over in the left-hand seat, and if you want our radiation readings, we just goofed. We left them all in the suits which are now nicely tucked away. We're going to get out Jack's suit in an hour or so anyway, and we'll get his dosimeter out if you wanted to get the reading on that one.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay, Jim. That'll be satisfactory.

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Okay.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: And in exchange for that, the Surgeon would like to have a rough number of hours each of you slept and a qualitative verb to describe whether it was good, fair, or poor.

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Okay. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Okay, Houston. We had an average of around 5½ hours [garble]. [Long pause.]

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Jim, Houston. Your comm got pretty garbled there just as you started to talk. [Long pause.]

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Okay. Houston, Apollo 13.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay, 13. You're loud and clear again.

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: We averaged about 5½ hours sleep apiece, and we're estimating that the sleep was good.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay. Copy that. [Pause.] Let's see what else we got for you, Jim. Midcourse-2 looks like about 23 feet per second [7 m/s], approximately retrograde and on time. And it's holding real firm there. For your information, and you don't need to copy this down, because it's still pretty soft, but we have an S-IVB impact of about 8.57 south and about 33.9 west, which is a little west and a little south of the Flight Plan value. We have it at a GET of about 77 plus 51 which is just before AOS, and the LOI paths are a little bit late, and as I say, it's still pretty soft, and we'll be updating you with

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: That's fine, Joe. Just as long as it doesn't hit Cone Crater.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay. And I'll have a consumables update for you in a little while, and I have a small Flight Plan update for you sometime a little later on when you're ready to copy. There's no big deals in it.

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Roger.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: And, 13, Houston. We'd like to verify that you cycled the O 2 cryo fans. We saw the H 2 , but we didn't see the O 2 get stirred up.

a13_0231538.speaker: Swigert
a13_0231538.text: Yeah, Joe. We did and - kind of looked like we might have had a little stratification because right after we put them on, we had a Cryo Press light.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay. EECOM told me that might happen, and he was right.

a13_0231538.speaker: Swigert
a13_0231538.text: Okay, Joe. We're ready to copy a Flight Plan update and your consumables.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay, Jack. [Pause.] The Flight Plan update has a couple of items in it, and the first one we'd like to do is to update the T ephem values in the G&C checklist on page G/9-2. These are fairly small changes, but in case you need them, we'd like you to have the exact numbers. Over.

a13_0231538.speaker: Swigert
a13_0231538.text: Okay. Just a minute. I'll get it out. [Long pause.]

a13_0231538.speaker: Swigert
a13_0231538.text: Joe, was that the G&C checklist, page 9-2?

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: That's affirmative. G&C, page G/9-2.

a13_0231538.speaker: Swigert
a13_0231538.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay. On that page in line 04, column B, change the number from 03366 to 05253. Over.

a13_0231538.speaker: Swigert
a13_0231538.text: [Garble] 53.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay. And in line 05, column B, change from 11000 to 33661. Over.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay. That's right. The only other thing I've got for you, Jack, is three additional questions for the booster systems debriefing, which is to take place at about 25 hours, and we thought we'd pass these questions up to you early so you can consider them. Over.

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Okay. We're ready to copy.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay. The first extra is, and let me get the original question because this question says, "More specifically on item 2," and item 2 says, "Were there any significant changes in the noise vibration level during the single stage of powered flight? Specifically, describe your observations during the early S-II center engine cut-off, and approximately 90 seconds prior to TLI cut-off, you reported a high vibration in the S-IVB. We'd like you to describe the build-up of this vibration and its behavior through cut-off." Over.

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Okay. Essentially, what you'd like us to talk about is vibration sequence during the early S-II cut-off of the center engine and also describe the vibrations that we encountered during the S-IVB TLI burn. Is that correct?

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: That's it. Okay. The second extra question is for you, Jim, and it says, "Comparing this flight with your ride on Apollo 8, were there any significant differences in the powered flight environment?"

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Okay. We'll describe a comparison with 8 and 13 as far as powered flight goes.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Roger. And the last additional question is what did the ORDEAL ball look like during TLI? As you know, we passed you an update to that setting, and we'd like to know whether it was riding right on zero or what during the burn. Over.

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Okay. Will do. Well we'll describe the ORDEAL ball.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay. That's it, and that's the whole Flight Plan update. I have a consumables update now if you want to listen to that.

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Okay, Joe. We're ready to copy.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay. At 23 hours, the total RCS is 1121, quad A is 274, quad Bravo is 286, quad Charlie is 274, quad Delta is 287; and the cryos are as follows: H 2 tank 1, 83 percent; H 2 tank 2, 86 percent; O 2 tank 1, 87 percent; O 2 tank 2, 87 percent. Over.

a13_0231538.speaker: Swigert
a13_0231538.text: Okay, Joe. We got all those, and how do we compare them with where we should be in the timeline?

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: As I understand it, Jack, you're running slightly ahead of nominal in both those areas.

a13_0231538.speaker: Swigert
a13_0231538.text: Okay; real fine.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: No problems. [Long pause.]

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: And, 13, Houston. That's all the business I got right now. I have a little news plan of the day for you, if you feel like listening to that a little later on. [Long pause.]

a13_0231538.speaker: Lovell
a13_0231538.text: Just hold off a little bit there, Joe, if you don't mind [garble].

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Stand by one, Jim. You're coming in garbled again.

a13_0231538.speaker: Swigert
a13_0231538.text: Houston, 13.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay, 13; Houston. Loud and clear again. Go ahead.

a13_0231538.speaker: Swigert
a13_0231538.text: Okay. Joe. On the news, Jim would like to hold off a little bit on that, and I want to make a request to FAO, if he will at some time during the day, when we have a - get a Flight Plan update with those activities we agreed to make optional during lunar orbit and the few activities we were going to delete, I think that I forgot and left that card back during the press of suiting, I left it in the suit room.

a13_0231538.speaker: MCC
a13_0231538.text: Okay. Wilco.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Okay, Jack. I understand FAO's working on that and we'll have something for you later on.

a13_0231538.speaker: Swigert
a13_0231538.text: Okay. We're not in any hurry.

a13_0231538.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0231538.text: Rog.

a13_0234700.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0234700.text: Okay. Jack. We copy the angles. You can go ahead and torque them. [Pause.]

a13_0234700.speaker: Swigert
a13_0234700.text: Okay. Joe. The time of torqueing will be 23 hours, 47 minutes, 30 seconds.

a13_0235445.speaker: Lovell
a13_0235445.text: For information, Joe, we're all configured back again now to our regular seating positions, if you're monitoring us.

a13_0241602.speaker: Lovell
a13_0241602.text: Hello there, Houston; 13.

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: 13, Houston. Go ahead.

a13_0241602.speaker: Lovell
a13_0241602.text: Gosh, we had forgotten, but we'd like to hear what the news is.

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: Okay. There's not a whole lot to it. Well, let's see, we'll start with the - Let's start with sports, what the heck. The Astros survived 8 to 7, the Braves got five or six runs in the - five runs in the ninth inning, but they just - they just made it; and in the other important game of the day, the Cubs were rained out. I have all the rest of the scores, you can tell me if you want any of them. They had earthquakes in Manila and other areas of the island of Luzon. There were three tremors and they kept the buildings shaking for about a half an hour or so, and it was about a 5 on the Richter sc

a13_0241602.speaker: Lovell
a13_0241602.text: Maybe we could borrow some.

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: [Laughter.] Okay. Okay; West German Chancellor Willy Brandt, who witnessed your launch from the Cape yesterday, and President Nixon will complete their round of talks today. Brandt reportedly came to the U.S. to seek assurance from the President to go ahead with talks with the eastern European nations, especially East Germany, Poland, and Russia. Many air traffic controllers are still out, but reports indicate that they are slowly returning to work, and you'll be happy to know that the controllers here in the MOCR are still on the job.

a13_0241602.speaker: Lovell
a13_0241602.text: [Garble]

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: Go ahead.

a13_0241602.speaker: Lovell
a13_0241602.text: I said thank goodness for that.

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: Okay. Some truck lines are being struck in the Midwest, and the school teachers have walked off the job in Minneapolis. Today's favorite pastime across the - Uh oh; have you guys completed your income tax?

a13_0241602.speaker: Lovell
a13_0241602.text: How do I apply for an extension?

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: [Laughter.]

a13_0241602.speaker: Swigert
a13_0241602.text: Yeah, Joe. I got to - hey, listen - It ain't too funny; things kind of happened real fast down there, and I do need an extension.

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: [Laughter.]

a13_0241602.speaker: Swigert
a13_0241602.text: I didn't get mine filed. I'm really serious; would you...

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: You're breaking up the room down here.

a13_0241602.speaker: Swigert
a13_0241602.text: ...because I may be spending time in a...

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: We'll see...

a13_0241602.speaker: Swigert
a13_0241602.text: I may be spending time in a - I may be spending time in another quarantine besides the one that they are planning for me.

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: We'll see what we can do, Jack. We'll get with Recovery and see if we can get the agent out there in the Pacific when you come back. By golly, let's see. In professional basketball, the Knicks beat the Milwaukee Bucks 110 to 102, and Billy Casper is leading the Masters after 54 holes with a 208, and spring football practice is in full swing. And that's about all the news we got; the updated plan of the day for you guys, the uniform will be service dress inflight coverall garments with swords and medals, and tonight's movie shown in the Lower Equipment Bay will be John Wayne, Lou Costello, and

a13_0241602.speaker: Lovell
a13_0241602.text: Outstanding. [Long pause.]

a13_0241602.speaker: Lovell
a13_0241602.text: Houston, this is 13. Is it true that Jack's income tax return was going to be used to buy the ascent fuel for the LM?

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: Well, considering that he's a bachelor and hasn't got that deduction to take, yeah! [Pause.]

a13_0241602.speaker: Swigert
a13_0241602.text: Hey, Joe. I'm glad you brought that up, because I was really serious about that.

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: Okay, Jack. We'll - We'll - we'll take care of it. Tom Stafford says he'll get an extension for you.

a13_0241602.speaker: Swigert
a13_0241602.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: And Jim McDivitt says, "Yeah, now that you mention it, he forgot to fill the ascent stage."

a13_0241602.speaker: Lovell
a13_0241602.text: [Laughter.] Suspicions confirmed.

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: Should give you very good performance on descent.

a13_0241602.speaker: Haise
a13_0241602.text: We should have a lot more hover time, huh?

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: That's right. [Pause.]

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: Okay, crew. About the only other thing I've got for you right now is an update to your P37 PAD for Lift-off plus 35. This is a change to the PAD we gave you yesterday. The reason for the update is for weather avoidance in the mid-Pacific landing area at 70 hours, which is the return time for this PAD, and in case the question arises in your mind, we don't expect any problem there for the end of the mission. The weather area is 20 degrees south of your end-of-mission landing point, and it appears to be moving to the south.

a13_0241602.speaker: Lovell
a13_0241602.text: Okay, Joe. I'm ready to copy the PAD.

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: Okay. GET of ignition is 035:00; Delta-V T , 7883; Longitude, minus 155; and the GET 400K, 069:54. Over.

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a13_0241602.speaker: Lovell
a13_0241602.text: And, Houston, Jack's going to try donning his suit now for practice, himself, and when he gets it out, we'll give you a dosimeter reading.

a13_0241602.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0241602.text: Okay. Real good.

a13_0244149.speaker: Lovell
a13_0244149.text: Okay. We've retrieved Jack's dosimeter, and it's reading 02022. [Pause.]

a13_0244149.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0244149.text: Okay. We copy 02022 on the dosimeter, Jim.

a13_0244149.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0244149.text: 13, Houston. At your convenience, we'd like the LM/CM Delta-P reading.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Apollo 13, Houston. Over.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Houston, Apollo 13. Roger. We're thinking together. And we're here waiting for your call.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, you were a little broken up there, Jim, but I think it's getting better. We're ready for the launch vehicle systems debriefing whenever you are. [Long pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Okay, Houston; Apollo 13. You were cut out again; say again, please.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Roger, Jim. We're ready for the launch vehicle systems debriefing whenever you are. Over.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Okay. Stand by 1. [Long pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Okay, Houston; 13. In answer to question 1, the changes in the noise level occurred mainly between the first stage and the other stages - the other stages were about the same in noise level, very quiet, but the first stage, of course, was - made quite a bit of noise in the beginning but - which built up during the high Q, and then [garble] went quiet just after high Q.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, copy that, Jim.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: I might mention that the noise level during the first stage was not sufficient to be uncomfortable at all.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Roger. And I assume comm was okay.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: That's affirm. Comm was very good all during - throughout the entire flight. Much better than I expected.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Now, in answer to question 2, there was, of course, a vibration transient in the second stage that - due to the number 5 engine going out - which occurred shortly before the engine went out, and slightly after that then the S-II stage was very smooth. [Pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, Jim. I guess the significant point there is that you didn't notice the vibration before you saw the engine light.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: That's right. We - we noticed the vibration but it wasn't such that we thought something catastrophic was going to happen; it just started vibration and then the EN light came on, and then the vibration went away and the stage itself was smooth.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, copy that.

a13_0251056.speaker: Swigert
a13_0251056.text: Yeah, and that - it was all pretty - pretty short in span - just a second or so before and like a second afterwards, Joe.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Oh. Roger.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: And on the S-IVB, the vibration of the vehicle itself wasn't what [garble] second [garble] powered flight - a very high frequency vibration.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: That was - was that during - just during TLI, or did you notice that at insertion? [Pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Well, it was a high-frequency viola - vibration but more noticeable during the TLI burn than it was during the boost [garble] flight.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, I - understand. [Long pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Haise
a13_0251056.text: I guess the S-IVB vibration during TLI was there all the time although it seemed to - to grow to us as the burn progressed, although that may have been just due to the boost weight decrease.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, you called this about 3½ minutes, but I guess the thing was slowly building up throughout the whole burn. Right?

a13_0251056.speaker: Haise
a13_0251056.text: That's right.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, was it uncomfortable or did it cause your vision to degrade or anything like that?

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: No, it - it was not uncomfortable at all but I was recalling the ride on 8, and the S-IVB was more - much more smooth than even it was on 13.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Copy that. [Long pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Okay, now, in answer to number 3, we did not experience any unexpected transients except that all of us noticed the PU shift. We thought it was more pronounced than we had expected it to be.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay. Understand.

a13_0251056.speaker: Swigert
a13_0251056.text: Joe, on that. I guess most of every time that PU shift occurred we all - almost all of us glanced at the engine light. We could feel definite acceleration change.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Rog. Understand, Jack.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: And, during the high-Q portion of the flight, the Alpha meter, to my knowledge, never went above [garble].

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: In answer to number 4, we got a pretty good look at the thermal shroud and the IU after taking the LM away, and from our viewpoint, the shroud was completely intact. I saw no loose particles or parts of it floating at all.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, Jim. Understand. [Pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: And, I guess we answered number 5. I don't think at any time did we have any communication problem during powered flight.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: In answer to number 6, the answer is essentially no. We saw no venting or suspected leak on the LM or the CSM.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, Jim. I guess you described to us the nonpropulsive venting on the S-IVB after the APS maneuver and we copied that at the time. [Pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Okay. Fred saw the S-IVB venting.

a13_0251056.speaker: Haise
a13_0251056.text: Yes, we had already talked about that, Joe. And that was also visible when it - of course, when it did its evasive maneuver when we were looking at it right close up.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Okay, Joe. The last time we saw the S-IVB positively was when Fred saw it venting at about - at about 5 hours. We think we might have picked it up later on. We saw a particle or something out there that was tumbling which might have been the booster or one of the SLA panels.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: And when was that, Jim? [Pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: We're - we're debating. It was somewhere between - say 7:30 and 9 hours.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay.

a13_0251056.speaker: Haise
a13_0251056.text: But, Joe, assuming the S-IVB is still stable. The object I was looking at was definitely tumbling.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, Fred. As I recall, it was stable then, although it's tumbling now.

a13_0251056.speaker: Haise
a13_0251056.text: Okay. It probably was the SLA panel I picked up.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Right. Incidentally, I guess the guys in building 6...

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Oh and I think we...

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Go ahead, Jim.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: I - I think we answered number 9. We - at around 5:32, I think, was when we think the number 5 light came on in the S-II, and a definite vibration which was more than just a high-frequency vibration we got with the normal S-IV burn, and then the light came on. I called ECO thinking from the training that it was 7:42 and looked up at the time and realized it was early. And then, soon after the light came on, the vibration stopped and the engine or the booster smoothed down. It was very smooth from there on. [Pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay. This may be a stupid question, but do you have any idea of what the frequency of it was?

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Only to say that it was much higher - I couldn't really guess now. It was rather a rapid longitudinal vibration. [Pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, Jim. Stand by now for a minute, we're going to switch omni.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Houston, 13, [garble]

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: 13, Houston. I read you. We still have quite a bit of noise on the loop.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: I'll stand by. Roger.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, Jim. It should be pretty good now. We copied you answering question number 9.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Do you want any more comments on the S-IVB vibration?

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: I don't think so. When you get all done, I'll - I'll make a quick check to see if the booster people have any - any additional questions. You skipped number 8, Jim; could you go back to that for a second?

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Okay, stand by. [Long pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Our only comment there, Joe, was that the burn on TLI, to our knowledge, was about 3¾ second longer than had been predicted and that was the only thing that we really noticed; otherwise, looked like V I was nominal at cut-off.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, understand. [Long pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Okay, on comparing the flight of 13 to Apollo 8, lift-off was about the same amount of vibration as I noticed on 8, but at the beginning of the flight, there was less of the sideways motion than we experienced on Apollo 8. The S-IC separation felt more violent on 13 than it did on 8, maybe that's because I was in a different seat, I don't know. But there was about three sharp transients of the cut-off and a couple of big bangs where we were thrown backwards longitudinally on our straps before the S-II went off. And the S-II was, of course, just as smooth on 13 as 8 except for the number 5 engi

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, Jim, got all that.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: The up - the update on the ORDEAL ball was a good one. At the burn, we were about - just about 8 degrees. We had to pitch down. The yaw was right on, all the way through the entire burn, and just towards the end of the burn, the ball started going back in pitch a little bit. [Pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, sounds good, we'll give Mike Wash a gold star on that one. [Pause.] Okay, Jim, stand by 1 while I see if we have any extra questions. [Long pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Jim, while we're waiting to see if they have any more questions, I'd like to read you the booster people's preliminary analysis on the - the S-II cut-off. Over.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: That's very interesting. Go ahead.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Okay, preliminary analysis of the data indicates that the center S-II engine vibrated at a somewhat higher amplitude than we've seen on previous flights, and it started at about 160 seconds into the S-II burn. As a result of these vibrations, the engine chamber pressure decreased to the level where the two low-level thrust sensors, the thrust-okay sensors, initiated center engine cut-off. Early evaluation of data indicates that no damage occurred to the engine, and the cause of the increased vibration amplitude is still under investigation. Over. [Pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: I'm glad it was the center engine.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Yeah, right. [Pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Joe, do you have any word on what marks we had for TLI?

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: At the time of TLI, as I recall, you had 6 seconds longer than the nominal burn which was 3 seconds longer than the 3-sigma low burn, and you were also Go for a second-opportunity TLI if we had required one. [Pause.]

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Okay, we were just wondering because it appeared to us that we had a longer TLI burn than had been predicted.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Yes, you did. We confirmed that - that - that cut-off time just about as you saw it, and I don't have an explanation for it, but it was within the 3-sigma margins.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: 13, Houston.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Go ahead.

a13_0251056.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0251056.text: Roger, we have no further questions. All the answers were clear and satisfactory, and we thank you very much. You can press on with the rest of your busy day.

a13_0251056.speaker: Lovell
a13_0251056.text: Right-o.

a13_0262908.speaker: Haise
a13_0262908.text: Okay, Joe. Out window 5, I just picked up the tumbling object again so, for sure, it must have been a SLA panel. I don't think we could still be in the proximity of the S-IV at this time.

a13_0262908.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0262908.text: I don't think so, Fred. It's several hundred miles aft of you. 700 miles is - is the number, I'm told. And since the SLA panel didn't make the midcourse correction, that might be it. [Pause.]

a13_0262908.speaker: Haise
a13_0262908.text: Yes, it's - I can't really tell for sure even through the monocular that it is, but it looks the same relative position to the stars. And the best I can tell, about the same intensity and still about the same distance from us.

a13_0262908.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0262908.text: Can you see it tumbling. Does it have a shape, or is it a point?

a13_0262908.speaker: Haise
a13_0262908.text: No. I can tell it's tumbling; I guess the flat side not only is facing me, it's not only much brighter, it also grows larger.

a13_0262908.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0262908.text: Okay. Very interesting. We'll see if we can figure out where that's at relative to you. They keep updating the S-IV impact on us a little bit. The last guess we had was that it'll impact about the same longitude we gave you but close to zero latitude and a little bit later. You still won't be able to see it. And they're saying it might make a...

a13_0262908.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0262908.text: ...they're saying it might make a 100- to 120-foot crater, too. [Pause.]

a13_0262908.speaker: Haise
a13_0262908.text: It'll - it'll still be past the terminator for us for a while.

a13_0262908.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0262908.text: Right. It will be at about the rev 20 terminator, so it will be late in your lunar orbit activities before you'll be able to photograph it, and FAO is looking at whether we can work that in or not.

a13_0264326.speaker: Swigert
a13_0264326.text: Hey, Joe? Is FAO ready to - or do you - or are you ready to give me those items that we made optional and deleted in the solo book?

a13_0264326.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0264326.text: Jack, we're not quite ready with that yet, but we will be before too long. Can you wait awhile?

a13_0264326.speaker: Swigert
a13_0264326.text: Sure can. I got lots of time.

a13_0275941.speaker: Lovell
a13_0275941.text: Just a passing comment, Joe. We're having lunch right now, and I just made myself a hotdog sandwich with catsup. Very tasty and almost unheard of in the old days.

a13_0275941.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0275941.text: That's correct, 13. As I recall the Flight Plan, you're supposed to put mustard on the hot dogs and not catsup, but I guess we'll overlook that.

a13_0275941.speaker: Lovell
a13_0275941.text: Ah, Pretty good. We have about four different methods of spreading catsup, right now.

a13_0275941.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0275941.text: Okay. Jack, we'll have your update to you before too long.

a13_0275941.speaker: Swigert
a13_0275941.text: Okay. Fine, Joe. We did a pit check on the Hycon camera and everything works okay.

a13_0275941.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0275941.text: Okay. Beautiful. We don't have anything else for you at the moment.

a13_0284644.speaker: Haise
a13_0284644.text: Houston, 13.

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: 13, Houston. Go ahead. [Pause.]

a13_0284644.speaker: Haise
a13_0284644.text: Okay. We'd like to get the FM up now to look at some inside pictures there.

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: Okay. Stand by and I'll get a Go on this. [Long pause.]

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: 13, Houston.

a13_0284644.speaker: Haise
a13_0284644.text: Go ahead.

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: That's acceptable, Fred, and meanwhile, when you guys are ready to copy, we've got an MCC-2 PAD for you.

a13_0284644.speaker: Haise
a13_0284644.text: Okay. Stand by 1.

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: Roger that. And also if you can go to P00 and Accept conveniently, we'd like to uplink. [Pause.]

a13_0284644.speaker: Haise
a13_0284644.text: Okay. You've got it.

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a13_0284644.speaker: Haise
a13_0284644.text: Okay, Joe. You can go ahead with the P30 PAD.

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: Okay. Here we go. MCC-2, SPS/G&N: 63634; plus 0.96, minus 0.23; 030:40:49.00; minus 0021.7, minus 0001.7, minus 0008.0; 080, 164, 326; N/A, N/A; 0023.2, 0:03.5 - We'll give you half a second on the burn time because it's so short - 0018.5; 44, 135.9, 28.1; and the rest is N/A. Comments: set stars 31 and 23; roll align 288, pitch 205, yaw 034; no ullage, LM weight 33499, and - Over.

a13_0284644.speaker: Haise
a13_0284644.text: Okay. MCC-2, SPS/G&N: 63634; plus 0.96, minus 0.23; 030:40:49.00; minus 0021.7, minus 0001.7, minus 0008.0; 080, 164, 326; N/A, N/A; 0023.2, burn time 0:03.5, 0018.5; 44, 135.9, 28.1; and the rest N/A. Set stars 31, 23; roll align 288, pitch 205, yaw 034; no ullage, LM weight 33499.

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: Roger. Readback correct. I have two more short comments on them, but I want to wait just a second and make sure I understand them before I pass them to you.

a13_0284644.speaker: Haise
a13_0284644.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: Okay, Fred; Houston.

a13_0284644.speaker: Haise
a13_0284644.text: Go ahead.

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: The two additional comments were just that, first of all, they biased Delta-V C by minus 0.34 feet per second based on your EMS null bias checks. That's just for information. And the second one also for information is that your targeted pericynthion is 60 miles [111 km] after this correction. [Pause.]

a13_0284644.speaker: Haise
a13_0284644.text: Okay, understand. For Jack's information, the EMS Delta-V bias is 3.4, and our targeted pericynthion after this maneuver is 60 miles.

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: That's correct on the pericynthion. The EMS bias is 0.34, very small.

a13_0284644.speaker: Haise
a13_0284644.text: Okay. 0.34 on the EMS Delta-V bias.

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: Roger. And...

a13_0284644.speaker: Swigert
a13_0284644.text: Hey, Joe, we'll give...

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: Go ahead, Jack...

a13_0284644.speaker: Swigert
a13_0284644.text: We'll give you - we'll give you the read - we'll give you the results of another null bias test for comparative purposes right before the - oh, at the proper time.

a13_0284644.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0284644.text: Okay. Real fine; and the computer is yours.

a13_0284644.speaker: Swigert
a13_0284644.text: Okay. Thank you. Going Block.

a13_0290004.speaker: Swigert
a13_0290004.text: Okay, Houston; 13. Are you copying the torqueing angles on the P52?

a13_0290004.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0290004.text: Okay, Jack. Give us a second. [Long pause.]

a13_0290004.speaker: Kerwin
a13_0290004.text: And, 13, Houston. We have them. You can torque them.

a13_0290004.speaker: Swigert
a13_0290004.text: Okay, Joe. Time of torqueing; 29 hours, 0 minute, 30 seconds.

a13_0292935.speaker: Brand
a13_0292935.text: Hey, you've got a new CapCom on now with the Black Crew, and we have about three items to give you, Jack.

a13_0292935.speaker: Swigert
a13_0292935.text: Okay. Stand by 1. Are these updates or what?

a13_0292935.speaker: Brand
a13_0292935.text: I'm going to give you some High Gain Antenna angles for TV and the rest is just information, general words.

a13_0292935.speaker: Brand
a13_0292935.text: Okay. Burn attitude for TV, your pitch and yaw angles are as follows: Pitch, minus 1 - minus 69; yaw, 180; High Gain.

a13_0292935.speaker: Brand
a13_0292935.text: Okay. Second point is that you're Go for MCC-2. Everything's looking good here.

a13_0292935.speaker: Brand
a13_0292935.text: And the last item's for Jack. Jack, preliminary indications are that you can get a 60-day extension on your - filing your income tax if you're out of the country.

a13_0292935.speaker: Swigert
a13_0292935.text: That's good news. I guess I qualify.

a13_0292935.speaker: Brand
a13_0292935.text: Yeah, we were just looking at the map, and you're south of Florida so you're not in the country now. [Pause.] But we wondered how about your car tags. Have you taken care of those?

a13_0292935.speaker: Swigert
a13_0292935.text: Yeah, I did, as a matter of fact. I think I did.

a13_0292935.speaker: Brand
a13_0292935.text: And, Apollo 13, Houston. Recommend Omni Alpha until you get to the burn attitude.

a13_0294032.speaker: Swigert
a13_0294032.text: Okay, Vance. The EMS Delta-V pass passive, the results of the no-bias pass in 100 seconds, have been from 100 to 101.5.

a13_0294032.speaker: Brand
a13_0294032.text: Roger. Copy plus 100 to plus 101.5, and that agrees fairly closely with the last one, as I recall.

a13_0294546.speaker: Swigert
a13_0294546.text: Okay, Houston. We're at P40 burn attitude. Jim is on the sextant star check, and we do have a star in the sextant.

a13_0294546.speaker: Swigert
a13_0294546.text: But we couldn't tell you whether it's 44 or not.

a13_0294546.speaker: Swigert
a13_0294546.text: Okay, Houston; 13. We're a little bit ahead of ourselves. Do we have a Go to do the fuel cell purge and the waste water dump? [Pause.]

a13_0294546.speaker: Brand
a13_0294546.text: Jack, that's affirm. You have a Go for those.

a13_0295014.speaker: Brand
a13_0295014.text: Jim, battery A is charged now. Whenever you want to unhook it will be fine with us.

a13_0301204.speaker: Swigert
a13_0301204.text: Houston, 13. Are you still planning to have TV at the scheduled time? [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Okay, 13; Houston. That's affirm. At the Flight Plan-scheduled time.

a13_0301204.speaker: Swigert
a13_0301204.text: Okay. All right. [Pause.] We've got a beautiful sight we want to show you. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Right. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: 13, Houston. You can go ahead with the TV now. We're standing by. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Swigert
a13_0301204.text: Okay. Here it comes.

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Okay. Jack. It's coming in, and it's right in the center of our screen.

a13_0301204.speaker: Swigert
a13_0301204.text: Okay, Vance.

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: Can you - Think you could guess what that might be, Vance? Better than Charlie?

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: I don't want to start flipping coins at this point.

a13_0301204.speaker: Swigert
a13_0301204.text: Okay, Vance. We're pointed just a little ways off from looking directly at the Moon. Jim is holding the camera through window 3. The Sun is coming at about 40 degrees off our left side, and what we are going to show you in just a minute is about 30 seconds of waste water dump and just show you just what it looks like. It's really fantastic.

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Okay. We'd like to see that. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Okay. We saw some droplets speeding out for a little while, Jack. Now we don't see anything.

a13_0301204.speaker: Lovell
a13_0301204.text: Actually, Vance, what you're looking at is solid water droplets coming out just about all the time. It lights up the whole sky around the Moon. It's just far too fine for you to see. Now I think they're coming out a little thicker.

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Okay. Yeah, we see those.

a13_0301204.speaker: Lovell
a13_0301204.text: Jack's complaining about seeing stars. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: FIDO says he can understand why that would perturbate a trajectory now. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Lovell
a13_0301204.text: It's amazing watching these little frozen droplets maneuver. They seem to go in all directions, but finally after they get out a certain ways, settle down and they all seem to be traveling about the same direction. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Right. That's coming in real well. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Lovell
a13_0301204.text: The objects in the foreground are parts of the LM that you're looking at. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Lovell
a13_0301204.text: The camera is now going to [garble]. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: We can just barely see those parts of the LM. They must be in a shadow. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Lovell
a13_0301204.text: Okay. Now you are looking at a thruster quad at the lower part of your screen.

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: I've got the f-stop all the way open now, Vance; that's quad [pause] quad 1 you're looking at with the LM should - The Moon should be in view just over the top of the quad.

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Right. We see the nozzle of the quad, but it's dark and it's not easy to see. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: 13, Houston. INCO suggests you try Average if you're in Peak to see if that gives us a better picture. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: Okay. We're in Average now. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: I think that helps out. We can see it better. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: MCC (probably INCO)
a13_0301204.text: Okay Flight. We - we shouldn't leave it there too long.

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Okay. Now, 13, request you either move it away from the bright area or else move it back to Peak. Over. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: Okay, Vance. I cranked the focus down a little bit. Is the quad coming in any better now?

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: It's coming in about the same, Fred, and you're a little weak now on the comm. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: We could see when you went back to Peak.

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: And I'm now zoomed all the way out. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Okay. We could see you zoom in on the Moon, and it's near the center of our screen, just a little to the left. Very clear. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: Yeah. I show it just about at 38.

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: We can't tell if it's gray or light brown, though. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: Do you have your grid down there, Vance? [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: That's negative, Fred.

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: I don't know if you can make out the features there, Vance, on the Moon, but it looks like the terminators are at central plains area somewhere around Descartes, maybe.

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Okay. We're - We see it just as a bright portion of the lunar disk, and it looks a lot like you see it from Earth. Very bright. We're unable to see any features at all. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: It's pretty much the same with the eyeballs in here, and it looks a little bigger now. But the only way I could see it very good at all was with the monocular, a little while ago. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Okay, Fred. Very good. We'd be interested to see in the cabin when you get ready for that, too.

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: Okay. I'll set up now. [Long pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Lovell
a13_0301204.text: And, Vance, we're counting down to midcourse-2, we're up to, in our checklist, to minus 6 minutes to go.

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Roger. Minus 6 minutes. Understand you're about ready to turn on the gimbal motors and all that sort of thing. Okay. We see the computer now in the upper middle part of the - the panel. I think we see somebody's checklist in the center couch. It must be Jim holding the checklist. [Pause.]

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: Right. And what Jim's holding now, he's got a pen in his hand we've rigged on a string, as sort of a simple-minded accelerometer. This burn's pretty short and I'm not sure even that's going to show very much. But we'll see if it'll stretch out at the end of its string.

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Yeah. We see the pencil at the top of the picture floating around. And Jack's coming into view now.

a13_0301204.speaker: Haise
a13_0301204.text: And I've gone back - Okay, I've gone back to Average now and [garble] the picture.

a13_0301204.speaker: Brand
a13_0301204.text: Roger.

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: Now in about a few minutes, Vance, I guess we'll see how about the only system we haven't used yet works. Everything else sure has worked mighty fine.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Right. The spacecraft's really working nicely. Okay. We're picking up panel 2 now. Still a little bit of the checklist. [Long pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: Just wondering if you can pick up the caution array there?

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Right. We just saw your - your testing of the caution and warning system at the left-hand side of the panel on our TV. [Pause.] See the lights all flash on. You're doing it again. [Long pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: You mission timer's showing up as a - a brilliant green in the upper left-hand part of the picture. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: Roger. I got the camera kind of canted on you here, Vance.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Vance, Jim's going to go to VOX now.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Roger. Read you loud and clear, Jim.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Okay. We'll - what we'll do - We'll be on VOX for the remainder of the burn and preburn countdown.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: [Garbled.] And what we're waiting for is 54 minutes on our counter or 20 which would be minus... [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Jim, we hear clipping on your VOX. Could you adjust it so that you're coming in continuously all the time?

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Vance, how do you read the CMP on VOX?

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Jack, read you loud and clear.

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: Is that too close, Vance, or can you make out the SPS engine panel now?

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: We - we can see your fuel and oxidizer gauges and hydrogen/oxygen gauges at the top of the picture and the PUGS, but it isn't coming in in focus too well. It's a little dim.

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: Yes. I think the problem is I'm about 2 feet and it doesn't go down but to 4. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Right. We understand that's the panel right in front of your face. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Okay. Vance, stand by for the main gimbal motors.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Fred, the focus is good enough that we can see the position of your four ball valves at the top of the picture for the big SPS engine.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: What would you like to watch, Vance?

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Hopefully, you'll see the - or we'll see the two on the left here, set A, go on here directly...

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Main Bus Ties, two, On, Fred. Okay. SPS Helium Valve, two, Auto and checked Auto barber pole. TVC Servo Power is 1, AC1/Main A; 2, AC2/Main B.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Okay. Rotational Power Normal no. 2, AC.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Okay. Let's do a primary TVC check.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Fred, are you ready to start primary?

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Good. Good trim control. Minus 0.96 - plus 0.96, minus 0.23.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: MTVC. Translation Control, Neutral. Max trim up to zero.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Rotational Hand Control Power, two, Normal, AC/DC.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Okay. BMAGs, you got three, Rate 2? Okay, we'll proceed for final trim. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: [Garble], Enter. Okay. We'll do the Gimbal Test Option.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Yeah. We can hear and feel the engine gimbal as we do the test.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: ...[garble] relay cut in and Trim is set.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Rate, High and update the DET.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Okay. We're coming up on 3 minutes. I'll give you a Mark.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: At 58, we want Delta-V Thrust A to Normal.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Jim, Houston. You're looking good down here. Go for the burn.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Translation Hand Controller armed. Arm your Rotational Hand Controller. I've got mine armed. Okay, Fred. Tape Recorder, High Bit Rate, Record, Forward, Command Reset. Standing by for 59. It's running?.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Standing by for Enter Enable. [Long pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Okay. Let's get the residuals. Okay, Houston, there are the residuals. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: On Low Bit Rate. Start. Go with the primaries.

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: ...is Off. Okay. Record the Delta-V C . You got that?

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Okay. You got the - You got the Delta-V C in minus 3.7.

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: I'm already in low bit rate.

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: Yes, we were on those [garble] so that we had less than 0.2.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Okay. Houston copied your residuals, very low.

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: Okay. Fuel is 1.0; oxidizer 0.25; the Ox unbalance is reading on the decrease, which doesn't mean very much, and I guess that wasn't too much for a push there, Vance. I didn't see the accelerometer do a whole lot and it was a little surprising how slowly the injector valves opened, at least on the indicators.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Roger. That was a very short burn. Request you give us a sweep across the panel when you get a chance, Fred. Let us see Jack and Jim again. Over.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Okay, Vance, I was going to show you on - wonder if the folks might - down there might be interested in how we find out how far we're away from the Moon. Going to do that right now in program 21 here.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: I'm asking the computer how far away we are. And the computer is telling me we're 121,490 miles out.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Okay. That agrees fairly closely with our map on the wall.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: I'm glad. That means you're tracking us too. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: And if you didn't see our residuals, it was 0.1 X, 0.2 on Y, and 0.1 Z, and Delta-V C was minus 3.8. [Long pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Jack, Houston. We show you down here 121 thousand miles 520 out. So I guess we all agree.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Okay. Real good, Vance. What I'm going to do is give you a shot of Fred. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: If we can get all the wiring out of the way.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: The big problem here is, when you move the TV around, this wire follows you like a snake here.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Yeah, we have Fred now. Looks like he has a lariat there, getting ready to rope the checklist. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: That's only half of it. We have most of it hidden away. [Pause.] It's been pretty interesting doing all the camera work here to get a little extra training running the TV here, hopefully for when we get on the ground at Fra Mauro. The monitor does make it pretty easy though. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Right. That's a real advantage in the cockpit. You're just a little bit dark. It looks like it might help to have the f-stop run down about one increment. See how it comes out...

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: Can't do it, we're wide open.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Yeah. We're wide open, Vance. [Long pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Okay. Does that help any, Vance?

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Okay. It's reasonably good. We can make out Fred fairly well. Looks like he's in a shadow. Hey, that helps. You just turned up the lights, huh?

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Yes. We went fixed on the...

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: We did notice one thing, Vance. You know that new fad with long hair? It won't work too well up here in space.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: I say, you know the new - the new fad with long hair?

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: It doesn't work too well up in space, you can't comb your hair up here.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Well, I guess you have to give up something. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Well, at least it - it helps to try. We can see you trying to comb your hair there, Jim. It looks like your - your beards haven't come along to the point where you've had to use the razor though.

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: Well, we've been debating that. We thought we'd take care of our beards tomorrow and make that one of our daily routines. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: I take it that was a subtle hint, Vance.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: No, no. We're not commenting on your appearance, Fred. I mean nothing derogatory, understand. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Lovell
a13_0302808.text: And, Vance, I thought we'd get a picture of Jack just so that all the girls know that he's still here. [Laughter.] Say hello to them.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Yeah, we - we appreciate that. There he is. Big Jack. [Long pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Jack, you're in the shadow right now; we have a little bit of interference from your window, which is very bright, so we can't - I think you're smiling, but it's a little hard to tell.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Hey, there we go. [Pause.] Incidentally, we've been getting all kinds of bits of information to pass up to you. We've had baseball scores coming in, basketball. Somebody said there's 220 days, shopping days left 'til Christmas. [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: Yeah, who won the Masters, Vance? [Pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: It was a tie in the Masters and stand by. [Pause.] It was a tie between Littler and Casper after 72 holes, and there's going to be a playoff Monday, we understand. [Long pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: One thing the world might be interested in knowing is what you do after the burn in the way of configuring switches back. We - We heard you go through the checklist. But, I guess right now, basically, you probably have all the switches back in position and you're in a mode to continue on with - Okay. What does the Flight Plan say? You're going to be doing cislunar navigation. So, Jack you're going to be down in the LEB. Is that correct?

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: That's right, Vance. Be going down there shortly. [Long pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Okay. The TV now is all but black. Looks like it must be pointing into a shadow.

a13_0302808.speaker: Swigert
a13_0302808.text: What he's doing there, he's trying to give you one more shot of the Moon, and right now I'm setting up to maneuver to the optics calibration attitude.

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: And what I wanted to point out, I don't know if it's apparent, but to show the advantage of doing all the dumps just before the burn, we're looking again at the same scene over quad 1 at the Moon. And now you don't see all the sparkly frozen particles outside there anymore. We've sort of run off and left them.

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Rog. We - We don't see anything out there anymore in the way of particles leaving the spacecraft. We'd suggest, maybe you zoom the Moon in a little bit again so we can see the shape of it better. [Long pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Okay. That brings the Moon in. We can see the terminator at the top of the melon-shaped disk.

a13_0302808.speaker: Haise
a13_0302808.text: Okay. Now you can see a few of the spark - sparkling particles going across the screen. Those are being emitted from the thrusters. Jack's maneuvering the spacecraft now. [Long pause.]

a13_0302808.speaker: Brand
a13_0302808.text: Okay. We can see those very poorly. Well, actually, they're coming in better now. It looks like little specks going from the upper left part of the screen across to the right, and understand those are from the thrusters.

a13_0305412ag.speaker: Brand
a13_0305412ag.text: Okay, 13; Houston. Just as an item of interest, advise your speed with respect to the Earth now is 4,667 feet per second [1,423 m/s].

a13_0305412ag.speaker: Swigert
a13_0305412ag.text: Okay. Thanks, Vance. [Long pause.]

a13_0305412ag.speaker: Brand
a13_0305412ag.text: Okay, Apollo 13; Houston. The Moon has been in and out of the - the - our screen here. Right now it's off at the bottom side, but we can still see the particles coming off from the spacecraft.

a13_0305412ag.speaker: Swigert
a13_0305412ag.text: Okay. I'll have to pull it out the window now, Vance. The Sun's coming up on the right side.

a13_0305412ag.speaker: Brand
a13_0305412ag.text: Roger. Understand. You...

a13_0305412ag.speaker: Lovell
a13_0305412ag.text: Do you want to see any shots down in the LEB, Vance?

a13_0305412ag.speaker: Brand
a13_0305412ag.text: Say again.

a13_0305412ag.speaker: Lovell
a13_0305412ag.text: Do you want to see any of the photographs or do you want the TV down in the LEB?

a13_0305412ag.speaker: Brand
a13_0305412ag.text: That's right, Jim. It'd be good to see what you're doing down in the LEB or the far corner of the spacecraft where the optics are. Might be interesting to describe what you will do in the next few minutes in the way of sightings.

a13_0305412ag.speaker: Haise
a13_0305412ag.text: Okay, Vance. First we're going to give you a shot of the sleep station. [Long pause.]

a13_0305412ag.speaker: Brand
