a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Okay. And we're getting a good picture of the LMP side with the DEDA over there. [Pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Swigert
a13_0551400.text: Hey, Jack, one question on the Command Module here. Do I - I have the DAP right now wide deadband. Do you want me to begin setting up narrow dead band and nulling the rates to start PTC again? [Pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Stand by, Jack. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: What I'm fishing out now, Jack, is another new piece of hardware that we're taking along this time as a result of some comments made on the Apollo 12 flight. [Pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: What Fred is opening up - is a drink bag that we place inside of our neckring that will allow us to drink while we are on the lunar surface. They - Pete and Al - did not have that on Apollo 12 and they, consequently, got very thirsty. But we hope to alleviate that situation by having our own little bag of water which, with very little effort, we can have a sip or two while we are looking around and doing our geology work. [Pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: So if you hear any funny noises, it is just probably the drink bag. [Pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: Fred, the bag's empty. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: Fred's now looking through our optical device. It's an instrument in which to align our platform, and Fred is now looking into it just to see what kind of an outside picture he might be able to get. We might be able to use a TV camera to look through our optical instrument to the outside of the Command Module. A few minutes ago while we first came in, we did manage to look to the outside of the side hatch of the Command Module through our optical instrument. Stand by. We'll try to see what we can do here.

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Roger, Jim. Break, Jack, we'd like you to stay in the dead band you are now in, and we'll make a change when the TV is over. Another thing we would like you to do is check your pitch and yaw on your High Gain meter so we can compare it with what we're seeing down here. [Pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Swigert
a13_0551400.text: Okay, it's showing about - say 28 degrees and 267.

a13_0551400.speaker: Swigert
a13_0551400.text: 28 - 28 and 267. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: Okay, Jack, Have you got that picture now?

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Fred, about one-quarter of our screen is lighted, and it's impossible to determine what you're looking at right now. Maybe you could give us a little verbal description.

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: Okay. It's looking through the AOT in position 4, right rear. And we're looking back toward the - over the side hatch at the aft side of the service module. [Pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: Okay. It's a - is it too dark a picture, Jack? You think the f-stop open may help?

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: No, Fred, it's got to be centered up a little bit. That's primarily what you have to do.

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: Jack, we can't center it up any more, because the side hatch is only in one part of the AOT. The rest of that blackness you see is really space. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: Okay. We'll try another one, and it's a little better centered. In fact, the only other one we have that shows the whole picture. We're in the forward detent of the AOT now, position 2, and you should be seeing something familiar like a radar antenna. [Pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Okay, we see you moving the camera up to the AOT lens, and we got a real good picture now. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: And... [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: Okay, Jack, I'm looking out the right window now, and not too far off in the distance now, you can see the objective, and I'll zoom in on it here a little and see if it brings it in better. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: And it's actually beginning to look a little bigger now. You can see quite distinctly some of the features with the naked eye. And so far, I guess I have to even agree with Jim that it's still looking pretty gray with white spots. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Okay, Fred. We're getting a good picture of your destination there. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: Jack, you've been looking at the - at Fred's workshop now, and you can see the abort guidance computer. And over there on the - tucked away in his armrest, is our activation checklist, which we'll be using very shortly. Up on the top of the window, we have our camera already mounted ready for photographing the descent. And now Fred's engaged in his favorite pastime, I found out on this flight so far. [Pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: He's not in the food locker, is he?

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: That's his second favorite pastime. He's rigging his hammock for sleep on the lunar surface now to find out - to see what it's going to be like.

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Roger. Sleeping and then eating. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: Yeah, it's kind of difficult here, Jack, getting into a hammock in zero g. I'm not sure if I keep floating away from it or it keeps moving away from me. [Pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: If you notice a few things floating around, we found just about one or two washers occasionally.

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: And for the benefit of those that may wonder where Jim sleeps. Be a little difficult to rig his hammock in here right now with the hatch open, but his runs laterally in this direction, fore-aft. So he has the upper berth and I get the lower berth. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: And now while Fred's taking his hammock down and restowing it, I might give you some idea of what sort of confusion of attitudes since there is no up or down, and I'm situated on top of the ascent engine just at the entrance to the tunnel. I'll reverse the camera 180 degrees and go from Fred, look through the tunnel again back at Odyssey, and we might pick up part of Jack. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: There he is. We see him. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: Okay, Houston. For the benefit of the television viewers, we've just about completed our little inspection of Aquarius, and now we're proceeding through the hatchy-gap into the tunnel and going back toward the Odyssey. [Pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Okay, Jim. It's been a great show so far. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: And finally, Jack's let me back into the Odyssey as we slide on through the tunnel here. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: Houston, 13. Are you still on TV?

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Yeah, we sure are. We've got a good picture of the skipper there.

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: Okay. What we can show you now, a little added benefit, we've got the drogue on Fred's couch in the Command Module right now, we stowed it temporarily while we're checking out the - out Aquarius and underneath his couch, we've got the probe stowed. Quite a big cumbersome device, and we'll get a shot of it for you. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: You're looking now at our probe, the place on the nose of Odyssey. It's a very heavy thing but, of course, in zero gravity it weighs nothing, and it's much easier to move around. As a matter of fact, both Fred and Jack commented, as many people in the past have, of how much bigger the spacecraft appears in actual flight when you have such ease of movement compared to our simulators which make training rather difficult. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Okay. We're seeing a good picture of the probe there, Jim, and looks like the characters shaved before the show this time.

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: Well, Fred said he had to keep up his TV image.

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: Yeah. That may be my first and last time though, Jack.

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: It took Fred one hour to shave. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: We might give you a quick - a quick shot of our entertainment on board the spacecraft, which has been keeping us company for some time. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: This little tape recorder has been a big benefit - has been a big benefit to us in passing some of our time away on our transit to the Moon, and it's rather odd to see it floating like this in Odyssey while it's playing the theme from '2001'. And, of course, the tapes wouldn't be complete without 'Aquarius'. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Okay, Jim. We're seeing the tape recorder now, and just - by the way, how long do you expect to keep the TV on this evening?

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: Well, when we - Stand by one.

a13_0551400.speaker: Haise
a13_0551400.text: Yeah, I got them with the cabin repress valve again there, Jack.

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: Every time he does that our hearts - our hearts jump in our mouth. And, Jack, any time you want to terminate TV, we're all set to go. [Long pause.]

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Okay, Jim. It's been a real good TV show. We think we ought to conclude it from here now. What do you think?

a13_0551400.speaker: Lovell
a13_0551400.text: Roger. Sounds good. And this is the crew of Apollo 13 wishing everybody there a nice evening, and we're just about ready to close out our inspection of Aquarius and get back for a pleasant evening in Odyssey. Good night.

a13_0551400.speaker: Lousma
a13_0551400.text: Thank you, 13.

a13_0553900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a13_0553900-pao.text: That's Jim Lovell now pointing the camera at Jack Swigert in Odyssey. We're at 55 hours, 38 minutes into the flight of Apollo 13.

a13_0553900-pao.speaker: Lousma
a13_0553900-pao.text: Okay, Jim. It's been a great show so far. [Long pause.]

a13_0553900-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a13_0553900-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 55 hours, 39 minutes now into the flight. We presently show Odyssey and Aquarius at an altitude of 175,552 nautical miles [325,122 km]. Now traveling at a speed of 3,171 feet per second [967 m/s]. Although we copied no voice confirmation as to exactly when spacecraft commander Jim Lovell first went inside Aquarius, the Flight Plan called for a - for an ingress time of 54 hours, 30 minutes and we assumed that this occurred around that time.

a13_0554840.speaker: Lousma
a13_0554840.text: Apollo 13, Houston. The next thing we'd like you to do is to...

a13_0554840.speaker: Lousma
a13_0554840.text: ...we'd like you to roll right to 060 and null your rates for photography of the Comet Bennett. To do that, we'd like you to enable quads C and D. For the maneuver, use all your quads. And in precisely 1 minute, we'd like you to terminate the battery charge on battery B. One other request, we'd like to have you verify...

a13_0554840.speaker: Lousma
a13_0554840.text: One other request, we'd like you to verify your High Gain configuration. We'd like to know what track mode, what servo, and what beam width. [Pause.]

a13_0554840.speaker: Swigert
a13_0554840.text: Okay, Jack, during the TV, we were Auto Track, Narrow Beam Width, and the Primary Electronics. And we had a good lockup. Just after we started the maneuver, I was able to lock you up and get real good signal strength, and it just seemed that right there at about 239 degrees in yaw, that the signal strength would just drop off and yaw would go to zero and pitch would go to 90.

a13_0554840.speaker: Lousma
a13_0554840.text: Roger. We copy, and the TV show was great.

a13_0554840.speaker: Swigert
a13_0554840.text: Okay, real fine. Okay, I'm going to maneuver to 060, 090, and 0. [Pause.]

a13_0554840.speaker: Lousma
a13_0554840.text: And, 13, we'd like to - to check C-4 thruster. [Long pause.]

a13_0554840.speaker: Swigert
a13_0554840.text: Okay, Jack. The battery charge has been terminated on the battery B.

a13_0554840.speaker: Lousma
a13_0554840.text: Roger. We see it, Jack. And we got a reading of minus 2 degrees on the docking index. We'd like to know if that's 2.0 precise or if it's 2.1 or 1.9.

a13_0554840.speaker: Lousma
a13_0554840.text: 13, we've got one more item for you, when you get a chance. We'd like you to stir up your cryo tanks. In addition, I have shaft and trunnion... [Pause.]

a13_0554840.speaker: Lousma
a13_0554840.text: ...for looking at the Comet Bennett, if you need it.

a13_0555519.speaker: Swigert
a13_0555519.text: Okay, Houston...

a13_0555519.speaker: Lovell
a13_0555519.text: ...Houston...

a13_0555519.speaker: Swigert
a13_0555519.text: ...we've had a problem here. [Pause.]

a13_0555519.speaker: Fenner (GUIDO)
a13_0555519.text: FLIGHT, GUIDANCE.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Go GUIDANCE.

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: This is Houston. Say again, please.

a13_0555519.speaker: Fenner (GUIDO)
a13_0555519.text: We've had a Hardware Restart. I don't know what it was.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Okay. GNC, you want to take a look at it? See if you see any problems?

a13_0555519.speaker: Lovell
a13_0555519.text: [Garble.] Ah, Houston, we've had a problem. We've had a Main B Bus Undervolt.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Roger, we're copying it, CapCom. We see a hardware restart.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: You see an AC Bus Undervolt there, GUIDANCE - ehhhm EECOM?

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: Roger. Main B Undervolt. [Long pause.]

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: Negative, FLIGHT

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: I believe the crew reported it.

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma (CAPCOM)
a13_0555519.text: We've got a Main Bus B undervolt.

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: Okay, flight, we've got some instrumentation funnies. Let me add them up.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Roger.

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: Okay, stand by, 13. We're looking at it. [Pause.]

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: We may have had an instrumentation problem, FLIGHT.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Rog.

a13_0555519.speaker: Glines (INCO)
a13_0555519.text: FLIGHT, INCO.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Go, INCO.

a13_0555519.speaker: Glines (INCO)
a13_0555519.text: We switched to wide beam width about the time he had that problem.

a13_0555519.speaker: Haise
a13_0555519.text: Okay. Right now, Houston, the voltage is - is looking good. And we had a pretty large bang associated with the Caution and Warning there. And as I recall, Main B was the one that had had an amp spike on it once before. [Pause.]

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: Roger, Fred. [Long pause.]

a13_0555519.speaker: Haise
a13_0555519.text: In the interim here, we're starting to go ahead and button up the tunnel again. [Pause.]

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: Roger.

a13_0555519.speaker: Haise
a13_0555519.text: Yeah. That - That jolt, uh, must have rocked the, uh, the sensor on - uh, see now - on O 2 Quantity 2. It's, uh - was oscillating down around 20 to 60 percent. Now it's full-scale high again.

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a13_0555519.speaker: Lovell
a13_0555519.text: And, Houston, we had a Restart on our computer and we had a PGNCS light and the Restart Reset.

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: Roger. Restart and a PGNCS light. Restart on a PGNCS and Reset...

a13_0555519.speaker: Lovell
a13_0555519.text: Okay. And we're looking at our S - Service Module RCS Helium 1. We have - B is barber poled and D is barber poled; Helium 2, D is barber pole, and Secondary Propellants, I have A and C barber pole. BMAG temperatures?

a13_0555519.speaker: Haise
a13_0555519.text: Okay, AC 2 is showing zip. I'm going to try to reconfigure on that, Jack.

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: EECOM, you see any AC problems? Looks like...

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: FLIGHT, EECOM.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: ...we've got a lot of instrumentation problems here. Go ahead.

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: That's affirm. He's flipping the fuel cells around, FLIGHT.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Well, let's get some recommendation here, Sy, if you've got any better ideas.

a13_0555519.speaker: Haise
a13_0555519.text: Yeah. We got a Main Bus A Undervolt now, too, showing.

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: Main A Undervolt.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Sy, what do you want to do? Hold your own, and...

a13_0555519.speaker: Haise
a13_0555519.text: It's reading about 25½. Main B is reading zip right now. [Long pause.]

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Sy, have you got a SIG sensor type problem there, or what?

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: FLIGHT, EECOM.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Go ahead.

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: He's got - fuel cells 1 and 3 are offline. We've got Main A volts, we have no Main B volts. Have them attempt to reconnect the fuel cells. Fuel Cell 1 to Main A, Fuel Cell 3 to Main B.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Okay.

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: Just try that...

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Fuel Cell 1 ...

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: ...back to Main A, Fuel Cell 3 back to Main B.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: ...Main A, 3 to Main B.

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: Let's see what happens.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Okay, now is there - do we have instrumentation problems?

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: Well, we've lost A - it does appear we've lost AC Bus 2 Voltage. Main B is reading - 4 volts. And that effectively takes AC 2 away from us...

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Okay.

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: ...the - yeah and he reported barber poles on the...

a13_0555519.speaker: Lovell
a13_0555519.text: And, Houston, Odyssey.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Rog.

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: ...on the fuel cell onboard, too, FLIGHT.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Yeah...

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: Stand by one, Jim. [Long pause.]

a13_0555519.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0555519.text: FLIGHT, GNC.

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: Let's see if we can get our DC back.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Rog. Go ahead, GNC.

a13_0555519.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0555519.text: Verify that the Quad Delta Helium Valves are Open.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: You seeing an attitude problem or you seeing some BI-levels that are giving you problems?

a13_0555519.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0555519.text: [Under Kranz.] No.

a13_0555519.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0555519.text: No, it's some low pressures in the fuel and oxidizer which would be symptomatic of the Helium Valve closing and firing some jets.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Quad number 2 helium valve, Open?

a13_0555519.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0555519.text: Quad Delta.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Quad Delta - Helium Valve, Open, right?

a13_0555519.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0555519.text: Right.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: CAPCOM, do you want to verify that quad Delta Helium Valve is Open, please.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Are there other problems in the RCS, Buck?

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma (CAPCOM)
a13_0555519.text: Okay, is that all we've come up with for them; have we got any other recommendations?

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Yeah, we wanted to get Fuel Cell 1 configured to Main A, Fuel Cell 3 to Main B. Did you pass that up?

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: Let's attempt that, FLIGHT.

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: 13, Houston. We'd like you to attempt to reconnect fuel cell 1 to Main A and fuel cell 3 to Main B. Verify that quad Delta is open. [Pause.]

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: INCO, this seems to be AC type problem, may be tied into that High Gain thing you got.

a13_0555519.speaker: Scott (INCO)
a13_0555519.text: We went - went to Wide Beam Width, FLIGHT, at 55:55:04, as best as we can tell.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Okay.

a13_0555519.speaker: Haise
a13_0555519.text: Okay, Houston. I'm showing - I tried to reset and fuel cell 1 and 3 are both showing gray flags, but they're both showing zip on the flows.

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: I copy, FLIGHT.

a13_0555519.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0555519.text: Let me commiserate on that.

a13_0555519.speaker: Lousma
a13_0555519.text: We copy.

a13_0555519.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0555519.text: Is there any kind of leads we can give them? Are we looking at instrumentation or have we got a real problem, or what?

a13_0560317.speaker: Swigert
a13_0560317.text: Okay, Houston. Are you still reading 13?

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: That's affirmative. We're reading you. We're trying to come up with some good ideas here for you.

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: Say again, Fred.

a13_0560317.speaker: Haise
a13_0560317.text: In the interim, to help out Main A voltage, I've got Main Bus Tie Bat AC, On. Or would you rather accept the 25 volts we're seeing on Main A?

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: Okay. Bus Tie AC, On. [Long pause.]

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: 13, Houston. We need Omni Charlie, please. [Pause.]

a13_0560317.speaker: Haise
a13_0560317.text: You got it.

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: 13, Houston. We'd like you to verify couple of readings for us. We would like the nitrogen pressure on fuel cell 1. We need the oxygen pressure on fuel cell 2.

a13_0560317.speaker: Fenner (GUIDO)
a13_0560317.text: FLIGHT, GUIDANCE.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Go Guidance.

a13_0560317.speaker: Fenner (GUIDO)
a13_0560317.text: Uh, When hi - when his hardware restart, he was doing a predefined maneuver and, uh, that should have killed it but we're still moving. We ought to stop it.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Are we using RCS now, Buck?

a13_0560317.speaker: Haise
a13_0560317.text: Okay. Nitrogen on 1 and oxygen on 2. Is that correct?

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: Negative. Oxygen on 3.

a13_0560317.speaker: Haise
a13_0560317.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: GNC from FLIGHT.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: GNC from FLIGHT.

a13_0560317.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0560317.text: GNC.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Did you see any problems in Quad D Helium valve? Does that look like that's cleared up?

a13_0560317.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0560317.text: Rog, that cleared up, Flight, we're in good shape there.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Okay, now, are we using RCS now?

a13_0560317.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0560317.text: That's affirmative, we're going to have to switch some thrusters over to Main A to hold attitude here.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Okay. Aaaah... how much RCS we've used?

a13_0560317.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0560317.text: Oh, We've used um - our guess 25 pounds.

a13_0560317.speaker: Haise
a13_0560317.text: Okay. Systems test 1-A says zip. [Long pause.]

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Okay. Give me a minimum fuel usage configuration that'll keep me attitude.

a13_0560317.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0560317.text: Rog.

a13_0560317.speaker: Heselmeyer (TELMU)
a13_0560317.text: FLIGHT, TELMU.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Go, TELMU.

a13_0560317.speaker: Heselmeyer (TELMU)
a13_0560317.text: The LM heater current's become essentially static.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Rog. Let's solve one problem at a time. Come back to me later on on it.

a13_0560317.speaker: Haise
a13_0560317.text: And 2-Baker, which is 3 oxygen, says 0.6.

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: 2 Baker says 0.6, and say again the other one.

a13_0560317.speaker: Haise
a13_0560317.text: Fuel cell 1 nitrogen reads zero.

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: Roger. Zero.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Okay, Sy - give me your - next best thing to try.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: EECOM, from Flight.

a13_0560317.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0560317.text: EECOM, Flight.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Go ahead.

a13_0560317.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0560317.text: Uhmmm... why don't we try [sigh] leave fuel cell 2 alone and make sure that 1 and 3 are disconnected from the buses and make sure there's absolutely no load on them at all and - see what happens.

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: 13, Houston. We'd like you to open circuit fuel cell 1; leave 2 and 3 as is.

a13_0560317.speaker: Haise
a13_0560317.text: Okay. I'll get to work on that.

a13_0560317.speaker: Lovell
a13_0560317.text: And, Jack, our O 2 quantity number 2 tank is reading zero. Did you get that? [Pause.]

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: O 2 Quantity number 2 is zero.

a13_0560317.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0560317.text: Roger, Flight. That's the AC problem.

a13_0560317.speaker: Lovell
a13_0560317.text: That's AC, okay. Yeah, that's - that's a - good with AC and it looks to me, looking out the hatch, that we are venting something. We are - We are venting something out into the - into space.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Roger.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Crew thinks they are venting something!

a13_0560317.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0560317.text: I heard it, FLIGHT.

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: Roger. We copy your venting.

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma (CAPCOM)
a13_0560317.text: Copy that, FLIGHT?

a13_0560317.speaker: Lovell
a13_0560317.text: It's a gas of some sort. [Long pause.]

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Rog. (Pause) Okay, let's everybody think of the kind of things we might be venting. GNC; you got anything that looks abnormal in your system?

a13_0560317.speaker: Willoughby (GNC)
a13_0560317.text: Negative, FLIGHT.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: How about you, EECOM? You see anything that - with the instrumentation you've got that could be venting?

a13_0560317.speaker: Haise
a13_0560317.text: Okay. Fuel cell 1, you just wanted it off the line now, Jack, is that right?

a13_0560317.speaker: Lousma
a13_0560317.text: We just wanted you to open the circuit on fuel cell 1.

a13_0560317.speaker: Haise (under Lousma)
a13_0560317.text: Open circuit it, right?

a13_0560317.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0560317.text: That's affirm FLIGHT. Let me look at the systems as far as venting is concerned.

a13_0560317.speaker: Haise
a13_0560317.text: Okay. She's off the line.

a13_0560317.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0560317.text: Okay. Let's start scanning.

a13_0561200-pao.speaker: Mission Control
a13_0561200-pao.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. This rapid exchange of conversation you've heard, may the main B bus is off the line, fuel cells 1 and 3 also off the line, fuel cell 2 is presently on the line. We now show 13 in an altitude of 178,643 nautical miles [330,847 km]. We're at 56 hours, 12 minutes into the flight.

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: 13, Houston. We see you getting close to gimbal lock there. We'd like you to bring up all quad Cs on Main A, quad C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4 on Main A, and also bring B-3 and B-4 up on Main A. [Pause.]

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: 13, Houston. Do you read?

a13_0561247.speaker: Haise
a13_0561247.text: Yeah. We got it.

a13_0561247.speaker: Lovell
a13_0561247.text: Affirm.

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: Okay. Can you tell us anything about the venting...

a13_0561247.speaker: Haise
a13_0561247.text: Okay.

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: ...where it's coming from, what window you see it at.

a13_0561247.speaker: Haise
a13_0561247.text: It's coming out of window 1, right now, Jack, and could you give me the thrusters again?

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: Okay, the thrusters...

a13_0561247.speaker: Haise
a13_0561247.text: What buses?

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: We'd like - on Main A, we'd like Charlie 1, 2, 3, and 4. Also Bravo 3 and 4 on Main A.

a13_0561247.speaker: Haise
a13_0561247.text: Okay. Got it. [Long pause.]

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: 13, we need Omni Bravo.

a13_0561247.speaker: Haise
a13_0561247.text: Omni Bravo.

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: Okay, 13; this is Houston. We'd like you to go to your G&C checklist, the pink pages, 1-5. Do powerdown until we get a Delta of 10 amps. Over.

a13_0561247.speaker: Haise
a13_0561247.text: All right.

a13_0561247.speaker: Lovell
a13_0561247.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a13_0561247.speaker: Lovell
a13_0561247.text: Okay, Jack, say again that - [Garbled] for the power-down; it's not in the pink pages, the 1-5.

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: Okay. We'd like you to go down that power-down procedure until you get a Delta of 10 amps. Over.

a13_0561247.speaker: Lovell
a13_0561247.text: Roger. Say - uh, never mind. [Long pause.]

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: 13, Houston. Did you copy our power-down request?

a13_0561247.speaker: Swigert
a13_0561247.text: Roger, Jack. We're - we're doing it right now.

a13_0561247.speaker: Lovell
a13_0561247.text: Yeah, where - Where did you say that was located, Jack?

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: That's in your systems checklist, page 1-5. [Long pause.]

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: And, 13, you might also check for those pages in your launch checklist. They're emergency pages; pink pages, 1-5, and we'd like you to power down until you get...

a13_0561247.speaker: Swigert
a13_0561247.text: Okay. That was must be in the launch checklist, Jack.

a13_0561247.speaker: Lousma
a13_0561247.text: Roger. Power down until you get a amperage of 10 amps less than what you got now. Over.

a13_0561247.speaker: Lovell
a13_0561247.text: Okay.

a13_0562206.speaker: Haise
a13_0562206.text: Okay. Jack. Are you happy with the amps we have now?

a13_0562206.speaker: Lousma
a13_0562206.text: Stand by one, Fred.

a13_0562206.speaker: Swigert
a13_0562206.text: Okay, Jack, and on this page 1-5, we proceeded right down the list, all the way down; we're right now at BMAG number 2 is in Warm Up.

a13_0562206.speaker: Lousma
a13_0562206.text: Roger. We copy BMAG 2 in Warm Up. We'll follow you through.

a13_0562206.speaker: Swigert
a13_0562206.text: Okay, and something is giving us a reach, Jack, both in pitch and roll, so I'm suspecting that maybe it's whatever it is that's venting back there. I've had to use Direct in order to stabilize this, and as soon as I do, we're starting to pick up rates again. Can you pick up any jets firing?

a13_0562206.speaker: Lousma
a13_0562206.text: Stand by. What direction are your rates in, Jack?

a13_0562206.speaker: Swigert
a13_0562206.text: It's negative pitch and negative roll.

a13_0562206.speaker: Lousma
a13_0562206.text: Roger.

a13_0562206.speaker: Lousma
a13_0562206.text: 13, Houston. We need to get some more instrumentation up. We'd like you to put Inverter 1 on both AC Buses. Over.

a13_0562206.speaker: Haise
a13_0562206.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a13_0562206.speaker: Haise
a13_0562206.text: Okay, you got Inverter 1 on both AC Buses now. [Pause.]

a13_0562206.speaker: Haise
a13_0562206.text: And Jack, one of the items that we turned off was the - all the fuel cell pumps. Okay, and you might let us know when fuel cell 2 needs its pump back; we ought to take care of that guy.

a13_0562206.speaker: Lousma
a13_0562206.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a13_0562206.speaker: Lousma
a13_0562206.text: Okay, Fred, we want Fuel Cell 2 Pumps to AC1, please.

a13_0562206.speaker: Lovell
a13_0562206.text: Fuel Cell 2 to AC1. Roger.

a13_0562206.speaker: Haise
a13_0562206.text: Okay, it's on AC1.

a13_0562206.speaker: Lousma
a13_0562206.text: Omni Charlie, please, 13.

a13_0562206.speaker: Lovell
a13_0562206.text: Omni Charlie. [Long pause.]

a13_0562206.speaker: Lousma
a13_0562206.text: Okay, 13. We've got lots and lots of people working on this; we'll give you some dope as soon as we have it, and you'll be the first one to know.

a13_0562206.speaker: Lovell
a13_0562206.text: Oh, thank you. [Pause.]

a13_0562206.speaker: Swigert
a13_0562206.text: Okay, Jack, and the weird configuration we're sitting in now is we have the hatch installed, we still have the probe and drogue inside the Command Module, and we're going to stay in this situation until you - kind of give us an okay to reinstall the probe and drogue.

a13_0562206.speaker: Lousma
a13_0562206.text: Roger. We'll give you an answer.

a13_0562206.speaker: Haise
a13_0562206.text: Or, if necessary, to use the LM consumables.

a13_0562206.speaker: Lousma
a13_0562206.text: Roger.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: 13, we'd like to have you put thruster Alpha 3 on Main A, please.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lovell
a13_0563211.text: Alpha 3 on Main A.

a13_0563211.speaker: Haise
a13_0563211.text: Okay, Jack, are you monitoring the quad temps in quad A - package temps?

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: Affirmative.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: 13, this is Houston. We'd like to power down just a little bit more, so let's get BMAG 2, Off; and make sure your lights are down. Over.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lovell
a13_0563211.text: Okay. The lights are down, and BMAG 2's going from Standby to Off.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: 13, Houston...

a13_0563211.speaker: Swigert
a13_0563211.text: Okay, Jack, now I've got a rate...

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: ...we'd like you to open circuit fuel cell 3.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lovell
a13_0563211.text: Open circuit fuel cell 3.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: Go ahead, Jack. [Pause.]

a13_0563211.speaker: Haise
a13_0563211.text: Okay, fuel cell 3 is off the line now. [Long pause.]

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: And 13, Houston. We'd like you to turn all your Bravo thrusters Off; and put all your Delta thrusters on Main A, please.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lovell
a13_0563211.text: All Delta thrusters on Main A and all Bravo thrusters Off. Roger. [Long pause.]

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: 13, Houston. Turn Battery A, Off...

a13_0563211.speaker: Lovell
a13_0563211.text: Okay, Jack, we've pretty well got the [garble].

a13_0563211.speaker: Unknown speaker
a13_0563211.text: [Garble] that down to nothing

a13_0563211.speaker: Swigert
a13_0563211.text: That's right; we were pulling current all the time.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lovell
a13_0563211.text: Battery A, Off. Roger.

a13_0563211.speaker: Swigert
a13_0563211.text: Now you have no...

a13_0563211.speaker: Lovell
a13_0563211.text: I'm transmitting. I don't have any current now.

a13_0563211.speaker: Swigert
a13_0563211.text: Hey, it's off - it's off. They - they killed the bus completely now. [Long pause.]

a13_0563211.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0563211.text: FLIGHT, EECOM.

a13_0563211.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0563211.text: Go, EECOM.

a13_0563211.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0563211.text: Have them isolate the surge tank also, and save it. We'll use the cryo as much as we can.

a13_0563211.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0563211.text: Uhh. Say that again?

a13_0563211.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0563211.text: Let's isolate the surge tank...

a13_0563211.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0563211.text: Why that?

a13_0563211.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0563211.text: ...in the Command Module.

a13_0563211.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0563211.text: I don't understand that, Sy.

a13_0563211.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0563211.text: I don't want to - I want to use the cryo as much as possible.

a13_0563211.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0563211.text: But that would seem to be the opposite, if you want to keep the fuel cell going.

a13_0563211.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0563211.text: The fuel cells are fed off the tanks in the Service Module, FLIGHT. The surge tank is in the Command Module. We want to save the surge tank in which we need for entry.

a13_0563211.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0563211.text: Okay, I'm with you. I'm with you.

a13_0563211.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0563211.text: Roger.

a13_0563211.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0563211.text: CapCom, let's also isolate the surge tank.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma (CAPCOM)
a13_0563211.text: Okay, you want to isolate the surge tank.

a13_0563211.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0563211.text: Yeah.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma (CAPCOM)
a13_0563211.text: O 2 surge tank, right?

a13_0563211.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0563211.text: Yeah. What we are really doing is securing our entry systems right now.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: 13, Houston. We'd like you to isolate your O 2 surge tank. Over. [Pause.]

a13_0563211.speaker: Swigert
a13_0563211.text: Surge tank off now, Jack? Okay, Jack, are you copying - O 2 tank 1 cryo pressure?

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: That's affirmative. And we're trying to get power to that tank. Stand by; we're working on it.

a13_0563211.speaker: Swigert
a13_0563211.text: Okay.

a13_0563211.speaker: Swigert
a13_0563211.text: Okay. We had a - Service Module RCS B light, Jack, due to a package temperature.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: Service Module RCS B. We copy. No problem.

a13_0563211.speaker: Swigert
a13_0563211.text: Let's read you the lights we got on now; Cryo Press, Fuel Cell 1, Fuel Cell 3, Main Bus B Undervolt, Suit Compressor.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: Roger, we copy them and we'd like to build up the pressure in O 2 tank 1, so turn the heaters on manually; we'll watch the pressure for you.

a13_0563211.speaker: Swigert
a13_0563211.text: Okay, do you want to see...

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: Go ahead.

a13_0563211.speaker: Swigert
a13_0563211.text: ...We're going to get a Main Bus A Undervolt, probably.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lousma
a13_0563211.text: Roger. We realize that; we feel we can stand 5 more amps on it.

a13_0563211.speaker: Swigert
a13_0563211.text: Okay.

a13_0563211.speaker: Lovell
a13_0563211.text: Okay, heater on tank 1's On.

a13_0564152.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564152.text: 13, Houston. We'd like you to additionally bring on the fans in O 2 tank 1, and we can stand the additional amperage on that.

a13_0564152.speaker: Lovell
a13_0564152.text: Okay - bring on the fans on O 2 tank 1.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: 13, Houston. We'd like you to check some circuit breakers on panel 226. Cryo O 2 Heater number 1, Main A, and check the three Cryo Fan Motors, Tank 1, three phases. [Pause.]

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: TELMU from FLIGHT.

a13_0564432.speaker: Heselmeyer (TELMU)
a13_0564432.text: Go ahead FLIGHT.

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: I want you to get some guys figuring out minimum power in the LM to sustain life.

a13_0564432.speaker: Haise
a13_0564432.text: Okay, Jack. 226 is configured just like it should be. I got three Reac breakers and three Rad breakers open. All the rest are closed.

a13_0564432.speaker: Heselmeyer (TELMU)
a13_0564432.text: Roger.

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: Okay.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Okay, Fred. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a13_0564432.speaker: Swigert
a13_0564432.text: Jack, looking outside, the number of particles has diminished greatly, almost ceased now, which indicates maybe what was venting has almost stopped.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Roger, Jack. Thank you. We copy.

a13_0564432.speaker: Swigert
a13_0564432.text: I'm still getting some rates in negative pitch, though.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: And, 13, we'd like to verify that both BMAGs are Off, please.

a13_0564432.speaker: Swigert
a13_0564432.text: Negative. We just have one BMAG. BMAG number 1 is still On.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Okay, Jack. Let's take BMAG 1, Off.

a13_0564432.speaker: Swigert
a13_0564432.text: Okay. BMAG number 1, Off, now.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: 13, this is Houston. We'd like you to give us a survey of your displays on MDCs 1 and 2. Give us gauge readings and talkbacks. Over.

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: See that juice is still going down there, EECOM. You got any more suggestions?

a13_0564432.speaker: Lovell
a13_0564432.text: Okay. We'll start with display number 1. Are, uh...

a13_0564432.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0564432.text: Flight, EECOM

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: Any more suggestions in trying to pump up O 2 Tank 1 pressure?

a13_0564432.speaker: Swigert
a13_0564432.text: Okay, Jack. On MDC 1, there is nothing abnormal. All the rate indicators are zero. Ball number 2 is, uh, frozen, of course; we lost - lost, uh. Main B. I've got Ball number 1 appears to be working normally. Right now I'm sitting at roll 0, pitch 180, and, uh, yaw about 13 degrees. I'm going to try and hold, uh, 0, 180, and 0.

a13_0564432.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0564432.text: No... (sounding exasperated) Uhh, FLIGHT, we're gonna hit 100 psi in an hour and 54 minutes. That's the end, right there.

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: Okay, 100 psi...

a13_0564432.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0564432.text: Less than two hours now.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lovell
a13_0564432.text: Okay, Houston. The center panel - I'm looking at the RCS indicator A. We have a package temperature of about 180. Our helium pressure is 3900. I'm looking at fuel pressure of about 180 and percentage of about, I'd say 85 percent. B is about the same, except that that package pressure is 190. On quad C, we're looking about the same, except that the package temperature is 100. On quad D, we're looking at package temperature of 160. All other indications about the same. CM pressure - RCS pressure is looking nominal. Helium pressure's up around 4000. And package temperature is about - a little les

a13_0564432.speaker: Lovell
a13_0564432.text: And the - talkbacks on the SM RCS, I've got Helium 1 now are all gray. Helium 2 are all gray. Primary Propellant all gray. Secondary Propellant, I've got two barber pole, and A is barber pole, B gray, C barber pole, and D gray. Okay. On the ECS Radiators, barber pole is gray. On the - On the ECS, Primary indicator.

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: FIDO, from FLIGHT.

a13_0564432.speaker: Haise
a13_0564432.text: Okay, Jack. Starting at the top. Okay. The Cryo Tanks; H 2 1 is reading 230 and the same for 2. Our O 2 Cryo Tank 1 is - looks like it's barely holding its own at 300. And Cryo Tank 2 is reading zip. Our quantities: H 2 1 is reading 73; 2, 74. On the O 2 side, we're reading O 2 1 at quantity 76; O 2 2 pegged to full scale high. RAD Temps Primary Inlet, we're reading about 55; RAD Out is reading about 30, and, uh, Secondary Outlet is reading...

a13_0564432.speaker: Stoval (FIDO)
a13_0564432.text: Go ahead FLIGHT.

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: Whatever planning you do, I wanna do assuming that we're going around the Moon and we're using the LM for performing the maneuver because in the present configuration unless we get a heck of a lot smarter I think we're wasting our time planning on using the SPS.

a13_0564432.speaker: Stoval (FIDO)
a13_0564432.text: Okay, FLIGHT.

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: So I think all of our return to Earth-type planning should be assuming the use of the LM DPS and/or RCS and I think third priority down the line should be CSM RCS.

a13_0564432.speaker: Stoval (FIDO)
a13_0564432.text: Okay, and I'm assuming you - you'd want fastest possible return?

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: Aaah, yeah, I think that's the case.

a13_0564432.speaker: Stoval (FIDO)
a13_0564432.text: Okay, we'll - we'll work on it from that side line, FLIGHT. Should be no problem.

a13_0564432.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0564432.text: FLIGHT, EECOM.

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: Go ahead, EECOM.

a13_0564432.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0564432.text: Okay, listen. There is a possibility that we blew a O 2 line in one of the fuel cells, and it's effectively manifolded there, of course. Now I'm - I wanna shut off one of the reactant valves to one of the fuel cells. And that would be fuel cell 3, since its O 2 pressure is gone. Now, fuel cell 1's oxygen pressure is trying to stay up there, at 45 psi. Maybe the problem is in fuel cell 3.

a13_0564432.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0564432.text: That sounds like a good assumption right there.

a13_0564432.speaker: Liebergot (EECOM)
a13_0564432.text: Yeah, fuel cell 3 is lost anyways, as far as...

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Excuse me, Fred; I'd like to butt in here a minute. We'd like to have Thruster C-1 off.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lovell
a13_0564432.text: C-1 is off.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: And proceed...

a13_0564432.speaker: Haise
a13_0564432.text: Okay...

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: ...my last copy is Secondary RAD In. [Pause.]

a13_0564432.speaker: Haise
a13_0564432.text: Okay. Your Secondary RAD In, I gave to you 70 - about 72 degrees; the RAD Out's about 30; the Glycol Evap Temp is reading about 65; Steam Pressure full scale high, Glycol Discharge Pressure about 9 psi. The Accum - Secondary Accumulator is about 30 - 34 percent. Our temperatures: Suits showing about 52 degrees; Cabin, about 58 degrees; pressures, Suit reading 4.1, Cabin at 5. Partial Pressure CO 2 is up to little over 1, about 1.1. On the SPS side of the house, the temperature is 72 degrees, helium's reading 3500; N 2 A is reading 2300; N 2 B, about 2450. And our ullage pressures: Fuel is read

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Stand by.

a13_0564432.speaker: Haise
a13_0564432.text: ...is 0 amps. Ah, Say again, Jack. [Long pause.]

a13_0564432.speaker: Lovell
a13_0564432.text: Houston, 13. [Long pause.]

a13_0564432.speaker: Haise
a13_0564432.text: Hello, Houston; Apollo 13. How do you read? [Pause.]

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Okay, 13. This is Houston. It appears to us that we're losing O 2 flow through fuel cell 3. So, we want you to close the Reac valve on fuel cell 3. It looks like fuel cell 1 and 2 are trying to hold up okay. You copy?

a13_0564432.speaker: Haise
a13_0564432.text: Are you saying fuel cell 1 and 2 - 1 and 2 are trying to hold up but we're leaking O 2 out of fuel cell 3? And you want me to shut the Reac valve on fuel cell 3? Did I hear you right?

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: That's affirmative. Close the Reac valve on fuel cell 3.

a13_0564432.speaker: Haise
a13_0564432.text: Okay. I'll go to the SSR page. Do you want me to go through that whole smash for fuel cell shutdown? Is that correct?

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Okay, 13. We want you to turn the inline heaters off on fuel cell 1. Then we want you to go through the fuel cell shutdown procedure on fuel cell 3. Read back.

a13_0564432.speaker: Swigert
a13_0564432.text: Okay. Shut down the inline heaters on fuel cell 1. We're proceeding with the shutdown, special subroutine, for fuel cell 3.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: That's affirmative. [Long pause.]

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: 13. Omni Bravo, please. [Long pause.]

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: 13, Houston. Over.

a13_0564432.speaker: Swigert
a13_0564432.text: Go ahead.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Okay. You got Omni Bravo and we'd like to have you verify that the tape recorder is off please.

a13_0564432.speaker: Swigert
a13_0564432.text: That's verified. Okay, Jack. I'm sitting here with an 0618 showing and I can't get rid of it here. Oh, stand by just a... [Long pause.]

a13_0564432.speaker: Lovell
a13_0564432.text: Okay. Fuel cell 3 Reac's are Off, Houston.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Roger, Jim. Thank you.

a13_0564432.speaker: Swigert
a13_0564432.text: Okay, Jack. Step 2, special subroutine 1 for the fuel cell procedure, has been completed.

a13_0564432.speaker: Lousma
a13_0564432.text: Roger. Thank you.

a13_0570429.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570429.text: Okay. Jack. I'd like to bring on jet A-4. I've got, uh, no - negative pitch control - negative pitch control, and right now neither Direct or Auto coils.

a13_0570429.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570429.text: Okay. You say no pitch in either Direct or Auto? You want to bring on A-4?

a13_0570429.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570429.text: Yeah. I got a - I got a positive pitch rate and I can't stop it.

a13_0570429.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570429.text: Okay, Jack. Bring A-4 on; stop the pitch rate.

a13_0570429.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570429.text: And, 13, we need Omni Charlie, please.

a13_0570429.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570429.text: And, Freddo, we'd like to have you, uh, verify fuel cell reactants talkback is barber poled

a13_0570429.speaker: Haise
a13_0570429.text: That's affirm. I watched it and it went barber pole as I threw the switch.

a13_0570429.speaker: Kranz
a13_0570429.text: Okay, all Flight Controllers, I'm handing over to Glynn. I assume the majority of all the team guys are pretty much briefed and up to speed as best we can. Now what I'd suggest is the White Team do two things. They go over the D-logs...

a13_0570429.speaker: Kranz (FLIGHT)
a13_0570429.text: Okay, let me go back over this again. We're handing over to Glynn. I'd suggest the White Team goes back and starts going through the D-log of the data. In other words, let's see if we can go back to the initial conditions and work on that problem to see if we can find out what happened and we may find some better clues as to what to do and let the fresh guys come on and try to figure out where do we go from here.

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Okay. Jack. Let me give you a thruster configuration right now. Able 1, Charlie 1, Able 2 are off. Charlie 2, Main A, all the thrusters that I call that are on are on Main A. Baker 1, Off. Dog 1, On; Baker 2, Off; Dog 2, On. Able 3, Charlie 3, Able 4, Charlie 4, On. Baker 3, Off; Dog 3, On; Baker 4, Off; Dog 4, on. [Long pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Okay, Jack. That thruster configuration looks okay.

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: All right. Okay. Do you want some readings from the Systems Test Meter regarding fuel cells?

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Stand by one on that, Jack. Let me ask the EECOM.

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: We've got some incompatibilities here. [Pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Okay, 13. We'd like to have you give us those systems test readings on fuel cell 1 and 3, please.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lovell
a13_0570801.text: Okay. 1 and 3 coming up.

a13_0570801.speaker: Haise
a13_0570801.text: Okay. Jack, 1-A is reading, lower scale, 0; 1-B is reading. 3.45. Okay. You only want fuel cells 1 and 3. Okay. Ignore that 1-B reading. 1-C is reading 3.4. Now, 1-D is reading 2.4. 2-B is reading 0.25.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Roger. Is that 2 Bravo, Fred?

a13_0570801.speaker: Haise
a13_0570801.text: That's 2 Bravo is reading - oh, about 0.25 to 0.3. [Long pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Lunney (FLIGHT)
a13_0570801.text: EECOM, I don't like the way that O 2 pressure's going down. If you want do something about these other reactant valves, let's make up our mind.

a13_0570801.speaker: Burton (EECOM)
a13_0570801.text: Okay.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lunney (FLIGHT)
a13_0570801.text: Don't you think?

a13_0570801.speaker: Burton
a13_0570801.text: Okay. Let me get back with you, a minute, FLIGHT. Would - Stand by on these readouts.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lunney (FLIGHT)
a13_0570801.text: Yeah, Okay. Anybody can copy the readouts. Be sure you - got discussing this reactants.

a13_0570801.speaker: Haise
a13_0570801.text: Okay. 2-C is reading 4.1. [Long pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma (CapCom)
a13_0570801.text: Hey Flight, CapCom, a long time ago I heard somebody mention something about closing a Repress package and then we never made a decision on that. Do they want to do that too?

a13_0570801.speaker: Lunney (FLIGHT)
a13_0570801.text: EECOM?

a13_0570801.speaker: Unidentified
a13_0570801.text: He's busy.

a13_0570801.speaker: Burton (EECOM)
a13_0570801.text: Go Flight.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lunney (FLIGHT)
a13_0570801.text: Uh, you want to close out the repress pack. I think that came on for 'em before.

a13_0570801.speaker: Haise
a13_0570801.text: And 3-A is reading 4.0.

a13_0570801.speaker: Burton (EECOM)
a13_0570801.text: Uh, we indicated earlier that we'd like to get it closed off, right.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lunney (FLIGHT)
a13_0570801.text: Yes, Jack.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Roger. 4.0. Say again what it is, please. [Pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Haise
a13_0570801.text: 3 Able, 3-A. [Long pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Burton (EECOM)
a13_0570801.text: Flight, EECOM.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lunney (FLIGHT)
a13_0570801.text: Go ahead.

a13_0570801.speaker: Burton (EECOM)
a13_0570801.text: Okay. On the reactants for fuel cell 1, uh, seems to me we have no choice but to go ahead and do it. The pressure continues to drop. Uh, we're not gonna have anything left soon anyway, so, uh, looks like the next best thing to try is to go ahead and turn the reactants off on fuel cell 1.

a13_0570801.speaker: Haise
a13_0570801.text: 3-B is reading 1.8. [Pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Haise
a13_0570801.text: And 3-D is reading 1.95.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lunney (FLIGHT)
a13_0570801.text: Is there any chance that I'm just looking at a bad pressure reading here? I'm going to shut off the second fuel cell now, is there any cur - any data you can correlate that say that, yeah, that pressure's going down?

a13_0570801.speaker: Burton (EECOM)
a13_0570801.text: On the O 2 tank?

a13_0570801.speaker: Lunney (FLIGHT)
a13_0570801.text: Yes. You understand my question?

a13_0570801.speaker: Burton (EECOM)
a13_0570801.text: Yeah, I understand your question. Uh, the temperatures are also dropping. Let me get a verification on that - stand by for just a minute.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lovell
a13_0570801.text: And, Houston, 13. O 2 tank pressure number 1 is less than 300 now.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Roger. We're seeing that. We confirm it. [Long pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: 13, Houston. We're going to have to have you go through the shutdown procedure on fuel cell 1. Our O 2 pressure is going down as you note and the temperature confirms it. Did you copy?

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Okay. Well, what bus configuration - What main bus do you want powered? [Pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Okay, Jack. We want you to leave the bus configuration as it is. Fuel cell 2 on Main A, and we need Omni Bravo.

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Okay, Jack. We're proceeding with the shutdown procedures for fuel cell 1. [Long pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: And, 13, Houston. We'd like you to isolate the Repress package, please.

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Okay.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lovell
a13_0570801.text: Isolate the Repress package. Roger.

a13_0570801.speaker: Haise
a13_0570801.text: I can confirm Repress package is off.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Roger. So now you've got the Repress package and the surge tank isolated. Is that affirm?

a13_0570801.speaker: Haise
a13_0570801.text: That is Charlie.

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Okay. Now, this is - We're ready to close the Reacs on fuel cell 1; is that right? [Long pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Jack, stand by on the fuel...

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: On that last - confirmation. Okay.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Roger. We're - We're giving you one last...

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: We want to just get one last confirmation.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Okay, Jack. We're getting that last confirmation. Stand by, please.

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Okay, 13. We verify that we want you to close down - shut down fuel cell 1, close Reacs valve.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lovell
a13_0570801.text: Roger...

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Okay.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lovell
a13_0570801.text: ...fuel cell 1; close the Reacs valve. [Pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Fuel cell...

a13_0570801.speaker: Lovell
a13_0570801.text: Reacs valve on fuel cell 1 is closed. [Long pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Okay, Jack. I can confirm step 2. The fuel cell shutdown procedure is complete for fuel cell 1.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Roger.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: 13, we recommend that you enable BD roll in the DAP. Over.

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Okay. Will do...

a13_0570801.speaker: Lovell
a13_0570801.text: Enable BD roll in the DAP. [Long pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: 13, Houston. We're working on the big dish now, so turn the High Gain Power switch, Off, please.

a13_0570801.speaker: Lovell
a13_0570801.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Okay, Jack. When we got the loud bang, we got also a restart. Did you copy that? Is - does GUIDO want anything, a Verb 74 or anything done with the CMC?

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Lousma
a13_0570801.text: 13, Houston. We're ready with a Verb 74 now, please. [Pause.]

a13_0570801.speaker: Swigert
a13_0570801.text: Coming down at you.
